body.text: 1. prathamaścittotpādaḥ
body.translated_text: 1. The First Arising of the Mind (<s>cittotpāda</s>)

body.text:
saṃskṛtabhāṣāyāmmadhyamakāvatārabhāṣyaṃ nāma /
(bhoṭabhāṣāyāmdbu ma la 'jug paī bśad pa śes vyava) āryamañjuśrīkumārabhūtāya namaḥ /
body.translated_text: The commentary on the <s>Madhyamakāvatāra</s> in the Sanskrit language. (In the Tibetan language: dbu ma la 'jug pa'i bshad pa shes bya ba.) Homage to the noble <s>Mañjuśrīkumārabhūta</s>!

body.text: madhyamakaśāstre 'vatārāya madhyamakāvatāracikīrṣayā sarvasamyaksambuddhairbodhisattvaiścāpi ādau bhagavatīṃ mahākaruṇāṃ buddhattvahetusampatpradhānām aśeṣāparimitāśaraṇabhavacārakabaddhasattvaparitrāṇalakṣaṇāṃ stutiyogyatayā darśayituṃ uktam /
body.translated_text: In order to introduce the <s>Madhyamaka</s> teaching, with the intention of composing the <s>Madhyamakāvatāra</s>, in order to show by way of its praiseworthiness the great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>) of the <s>Bhagavatī</s> — which is foremost among the causes and endowments of Buddhahood, whose characteristic is the protection of all beings bound in the endless, immeasurable, refugeless cycle of existence — praised first by all perfectly awakened <s>Buddhas</s> and by <s>Bodhisattvas</s> as well, it is said:

children.text: munīndrajāḥ śrāvakamadhyabuddhāḥ buddhodbhavāḥkhalvapi bodhisattvāt /
children.translated_text: Born of the lord of sages, the <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers) and intermediate <s>Buddhas</s> (<s>pratyekabuddhas</s>), and indeed the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> too are born of the <s>Buddha</s>;

children.text: kāruṇyacittādvayabuddhibodhicittāni heturjinaputrakāṇām // Madhy_1.1 //
children.translated_text: compassion (<s>kāruṇya</s>), non-dual understanding (<s>advayabuddhi</s>), and the mind of awakening (<s>bodhicitta</s>) are the causes of the children of the <s>Jina</s> (Victor). (Madhyamakāvatāra 1.1)

body.text: ityādi ślokadvayam / tatra anuttaradharmaiśvaryasaṃpadarjanāt, śrāvakapratyekabuddhabodhisattvebhyo 'pi paramaiśvaryasaṃpatteḥ, śrāvakādīnāṃ tadājñāvaśavartitvācca buddhā bhagavanto munīndra iti kathyante / tebhyaḥ śrāvakādīnāṃ janma tu tebhya utpattiḥ / katham? buddhānāṃ samutpāde pratītyasamutpādasya aviparyastadeśanāyāṃ praveśārthaṃ śruticintābhāvanānusāramapi yathādhimuktivacchrāvakatvādiparipūrttiḥ / yadyapi kasyacit pratītyasamutpādopadeśaśravaṇamātreṇa paramārthādhigamavaiduṣye satyapi dṛṣṭajanmanyeva nirvāṇaprāptirna bhavati, tathāpi upadeśasādhako vipākaniyataphalavat parajanmani abhīṣṭaphalaparipākaṃ niyataṃ prāpnoti / yathā āryadevena uktam- iha yadyapi tattvajño nirvāṇaṃ nādhigacchati / prāpnotyayatnato 'vaśyaṃ punarjanmani karmavat // iti // ataeva madhyamake 'pi uktam- sambuddhānāmanutpāde śrāvakāṇāṃ punaḥ kṣaye / jñānaṃ pratyekabuddhānāmasaṃsargāt pravartate // iti //
body.translated_text: These are two verses, and so forth. Therein, because of the attainment of the supreme sovereignty of the unsurpassed <s>Dharma</s>, because of possessing supreme sovereignty beyond even <s>śrāvakas</s>, <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, and <s>bodhisattvas</s>, and because the <s>śrāvakas</s> and others are subject to their authority, the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> are called 'lords of sages' (<s>munīndra</s>). The birth of <s>śrāvakas</s> and others from them means their arising from them. How so? When <s>Buddhas</s> appear, through entering into the authentic teaching of <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination), following hearing, reflection, and meditation, the fulfillment of <s>śrāvaka</s>-hood and so forth occurs according to one's inclination. Even if for some, by merely hearing the teaching of <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>, despite having the expertise of realizing the ultimate truth, <s>nirvāṇa</s> is not attained in this very life, nevertheless one who practices the teaching will certainly attain the ripening of the desired fruit in a future life, just as an action with a determined result of ripening. As stated by <s>Āryadeva</s>: 'Even if the knower of reality does not attain <s>nirvāṇa</s> here, he will certainly attain it effortlessly in a future birth, just like <s>karma</s>.' Therefore, in the <s>Madhyamaka</s> too it is stated: 'When the perfectly awakened <s>Buddhas</s> have not arisen and the <s>śrāvakas</s> too have ceased, the knowledge of the <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> arises without association [with a teacher].'

body.text: tarhi samyagavavādaphalaprāptikāraṇācchrāvakā iti / "kṛtaṃ me karaṇīyaṃ tasmān me nāparaṃ janma" ityādi bhavati / punaraparaṃ, satphalam anuttarasamyaksaṃbuddhamārgaṃ vā sarvatathāgatebhyaḥ śrutvā tadarthinaḥ śrāvaṇatvācchrāvakāḥ / yathā- saddharmapuṇḍarīkasūtra uktam-
body.translated_text: Then, the <s>śrāvakas</s> are so called because they obtain the fruit of proper instruction. '[I have] done what was to be done; therefore there is no further birth for me' — and so forth is said. Furthermore, having heard the fruitful, unsurpassed path of perfect awakening from all the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, they are <s>śrāvakas</s> because of their listening (<s>śrāvaṇa</s>) as seekers of that. As stated in the <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīkasūtra</s>:

children.text: adyo vayaṃ śrāvakabhūtanātha saṃśrāvayiṣyāmatha cāgrabodhim /
children.translated_text: 'Today we, O Protector, being <s>śrāvakas</s>, shall proclaim the supreme <s>bodhi</s> (awakening),

children.text: bodhīyaśabdaṃ ca prakāśayāmasteno vayaṃ śrāvakabhīṣmakalpāḥ // iti //
children.translated_text: and we shall make known the word of <s>bodhi</s>; therefore we are like formidable <s>śrāvakas</s>.'

body.text: sarve bodhisattvā api tathā, kintu tathā santo 'pi śrāvayanti eva, anurūpaṃ rañcamātramapi na pratipadyante, teṣāṃ śrāvakabhūtatvād bodhisattveṣu doṣo na prasajyate / ayaṃ buddhaśabdo buddhasvabhāvaḥ śrāvakapratyekabuddhānuttarasamyaksaṃbuddhān trīnapi samākhyāti, ato buddhaśabdena pratyekabuddhā ākhyātāḥ / te puṇyajñānayoru uttaravṛddhiviśeṣatvāt, śrāvakebhyo viśiṣṭa taratvāt, puṇyajñānasambhāramahākaruṇāsarvākāratādyabhāvāt sarvasamyaksambuddhebhyo hīnatvāt madhyāḥ / tasmādeva te upadeśaṃ vinā jñānotpādād ātmamātrārthaṃ buddhatvāt pratyekabuddhā iti / yathoktasvabhāvatvāt te śrāvakāḥ pratyekabuddhāśca tathāgatadharmadeśanātaḥ samudbhūtatvāt munīndrajā iti / punaśca te munīndrāḥ kuto jātā iti?- buddhodbhavāḥ khalvapi bodhisattvād ityuktam / nanu bodhisattvā api tathāgatopadeśata utpatrabhūtatvāt jinaputrā iti kiṃ noktāḥ? atoḥ kathaṃ buddhā bhagavanto bodhisattvebhyo jātā uktā iti? satyamidam, tathāpi hetudvayena bodhisattvā buddhabhagavatāṃ hetavo bhavanti- avasthāviśeṣatvāt, samādāpakāvatāratvācca / tatra avasthāviśeṣastu tathāgatāvasthābodhisattvāvasthayoḥ sahetukatvāt / samādāpakastu yathā āryamañjuśrīrbodhisattvabhūta eva bhagavataḥ śākyamuneḥ tatpareṣāṃ tathāgatānāṃ pūrva eva kāle bodhicittasamādāpako manyate / ata evaṃ tanniṣṭhāphalaṃ mukhyahetubhūtaṃ dṛṣṭvā tathāgatā bodhisattvajātā diṣṭāḥ / ataeva hetusampado 'tigarīyastvāt hetupūjākṛte 'pi phalapūjāyām arthāpattiṃ mattvā tairbuddhairbhagavadbhiḥ niścitam aparimitaphaladāyakamahauṣadhavṛkṣam aṃkurādisamudgatamañjuparṇāvasthābhūtavat yatnataḥ paripālanīyatvena darśayitvā tatsamaye āsannībhūtatriyānāvasaktasattvaskandhānāṃ mahāyāna eva niyojanārthaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ praśaṃsā kṛtā / yathā āryaratnakūṭasūtre-
body.translated_text: All <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are likewise, but even being thus, they do indeed cause others to hear, though they do not practice even the slightest [for themselves] accordingly; since they are in the state of being <s>śrāvakas</s>, no fault attaches to the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. The word 'Buddha' (<s>buddhaśabda</s>), having the nature of Buddha, designates all three — <s>śrāvakas</s>, <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, and unsurpassed perfectly awakened <s>Buddhas</s>. Thus, by the word 'Buddha,' the <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> are designated. They are 'intermediate' (<s>madhya</s>) because of their special distinction of greater development in the two accumulations of merit and knowledge compared to <s>śrāvakas</s>, being more distinguished than <s>śrāvakas</s>, yet being inferior to all perfectly awakened <s>Buddhas</s> due to the absence of the great accumulation of merit and knowledge, <s>mahākaruṇā</s> (great compassion), and omniscience. Therefore, they are called <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> because of their attaining Buddhahood through the arising of knowledge without instruction, for their own sake alone. Being of the nature as described, those <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> are called 'born of the lord of sages' (<s>munīndrajāḥ</s>) because they arise from the <s>Tathāgata's</s> teaching of <s>Dharma</s>. And further, from where are those lords of sages born? — It is said: 'and indeed the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> too are born of the <s>Buddha</s>.' Now, since <s>Bodhisattvas</s> too, being arisen from the <s>Tathāgata's</s> instruction, are children of the Victor (<s>jinaputra</s>), why are they not so called? How then are the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> said to be born from <s>Bodhisattvas</s>? This is true; nevertheless, by two reasons, <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are the causes of the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> — due to the distinction of stage, and due to being the initiators. Regarding the distinction of stage: the <s>Tathāgata</s> stage has the <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage as its cause. Regarding the initiator: for example, the noble <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, while still in the <s>Bodhisattva</s> state, is regarded as the one who initially prompted the arising of <s>bodhicitta</s> in the <s>Bhagavān Śākyamuni</s> and subsequent <s>Tathāgatas</s> in an earlier time. Therefore, seeing thus that the fruit dependent on that [initiation] has <s>Bodhisattvas</s> as its principal cause, the <s>Tathāgatas</s> are regarded as born from <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. Therefore, because the perfection of causes is supremely weighty, considering that the worship of the cause implies the worship of the result as well, those <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s>, showing that [the <s>Bodhisattva</s> state] must be carefully nurtured like the sprout stage of a great medicinal tree of immeasurable fruit-giving capacity that has arisen from seed and is in the state of tender leaves, at that time, for the purpose of directing into the <s>Mahāyāna</s> alone the masses of beings attached to the three vehicles who were near at hand, the praise of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> was made. As stated in the <s>Āryaratnakūṭasūtra</s>:

body.text: "tadyathāpi nāma kāśyapa! navacandro namaskriyate sā ceva pūrṇacandro na tathā namaskriyate, evameva kāśyapa! ye mama śraddadhanti te balavantataraṃ bodhisattvaṃ namaskartavya, na tathāgataḥ, tat kasya hetoḥ, bodhisattvanirjātā hi tathāgatāḥ / tathāgatanirjātāḥ śrāvakapratyekabuddhāḥ /" ata eva evaṃ yuktyāgamābhyāṃ tathāgatā bodhisattvebhyo jātā iti siddham / athavā te bodhisattvāḥ kiṃ hetukāḥ? uktam / kāruṇyacittādvayabuddhibodhicittāni heturjinaputrakāṇām / tatra karuṇā tu anukampā, atraiva vakṣyamāṇaprakārasvabhāvā / advayabuddhistu bhāvābhāvādyantadvayāpetā prajñā / bodhicittaṃ tu āryadharmasaṃgītisūtre-
body.translated_text: 'For example, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the new moon is saluted, but the full moon is not saluted in the same way. Just so, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, those who have faith in me should salute the <s>Bodhisattva</s> more strongly, not the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Why is that? Because the <s>Tathāgatas</s> are born from <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. From the <s>Tathāgatas</s> are born the <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>.' Therefore, by both reasoning and scripture, it is established that the <s>Tathāgatas</s> are born from <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. Now then, what are the causes of those <s>Bodhisattvas</s>? It is said: 'Compassion (<s>kāruṇya</s>), non-dual understanding (<s>advayabuddhi</s>), and <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening) are the causes of the children of the <s>Jina</s>.' Therein, <s>karuṇā</s> is compassion — its nature will be explained here below. <s>Advayabuddhi</s> (non-dual understanding) is <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) free from the duality of existence and non-existence and so forth. As for <s>bodhicitta</s>, in the <s>Āryaharmasaṃgītisūtra</s>:

body.text: "bodhisattvo bodhicittena sarvadharmān avabudhyet / sarve dharmā dharmadhātusamāḥ / sarveṣām āgantukabhūtāpratiṣṭhitadharmāṇāṃ jñeyamātratvād jñātṛśūnyatvāt parijñeyamātrāva-sāyitvena etādṛśīyaṃ dharmatā prāṇibhiravaboddhavyeti bodhisattveṣu yo 'yaṃ cittotpādaḥ sa bodhisattvabodhicittotpāda ityucyate / sarvaprāṇibhyo hitasukhacittam / anuttaraṃ cittaṃ , maitryā komalaṃ cittaṃ, karuṇatayāviparyayasaṃcittaṃ, ānandatayānanutaptaṃ cittam / upekṣātayā vimalaṃ cittaṃ, śūnyatayāvipariṇāmaṃ cittam, animittatayā nirāvaraṇaṃ cittaṃ, apraṇidhānatayāpratiṣṭhitaṃ cittamiti yathoktavat" / bodhisattvānāṃ mukhyahetustu karuṇā advayaprajñā bodhicittamitīme trayo dharmāḥ santi / yathoktaṃ ratnāvalyām- śailendrarājavanmūlaṃ bodhicittaṃ dṛḍhaṃ tataḥ / digantavyāpi kāruṇyaṃ jñānaṃ cādvayaniśritam // iti //
body.translated_text: 'The <s>Bodhisattva</s> should awaken to all <s>dharmas</s> through <s>bodhicitta</s>. All <s>dharmas</s> are equal to the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality). Since all [dharmas] are adventitious and without established nature, being merely knowable and empty of a knower, by virtue of being only that which is to be fully known, this <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature of reality) is to be awakened to by beings' — this arising of the mind in <s>Bodhisattvas</s> is called the arising of the <s>Bodhisattva's bodhicitta</s>. 'A mind of benefit and happiness toward all beings. An unsurpassed mind. A mind made tender through <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness). A mind of unerring conception through <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion). A mind without regret through <s>ānanda</s> (joy). A pure mind through <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity). A mind without transformation through <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness). A mind without obstruction through signlessness (<s>animitta</s>). An unestablished mind through wishlessness (<s>apraṇidhāna</s>)' — as thus stated. The principal causes of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are these three <s>dharmas</s>: <s>karuṇā</s>, <s>advayaprajñā</s> (non-dual wisdom), and <s>bodhicitta</s>. As stated in the <s>Ratnāvalī</s>: 'Like the king of mountains, <s>bodhicitta</s> is the firm root; then compassion (<s>kāruṇya</s>) extending to the ends of the directions; and knowledge grounded in non-duality.'

body.text: bodhicittasya advayajñānasya ca dvayorapi mūlaṃ karuṇayā bhūtatvāt karuṇā mukhyatvena deṣṭumiṣyate /
body.translated_text: Since <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion) is the root of both <s>bodhicitta</s> and non-dual knowledge (<s>advayajñāna</s>), compassion is intended to be taught as primary.

children.text: bījaṃ kṛpā yajjinaśasyarāśestadvṛddhaye vārisamā, cirāya /
children.translated_text: Compassion is the seed for the harvest of the <s>Jina</s> (Victor); water-like for its growth; and for long enjoyment,

children.text: bhogāya pākaśca yathaiva mānya, mādau mamātaḥ karuṇāpraśaṃsā // Madhy_1.2 //
children.translated_text: its ripening is like a harvest — therefore, at the outset, my praise is of compassion. (Madhyamakāvatāra 1.2)

body.text: yathā bāhyadhānyādisampattaye ādau madhye 'nte ca bījajalapākānāṃ mukhyatayā eva bhūtatvād upayogitābhāvaḥ, tathā karuṇāyā eva trikāle 'pi jinaśasyasampade upayogitāṃ evaṃ deśitā vartate / evaṃ dayālustu paraduḥkhaduḥkhita eva aśeṣaduḥkhībhūtasattvānāṃ paritrāṇāya "avaśyam aham samastamamuṃ lokaṃ duḥkhataḥ samuddhṛtya buddhatva eva saṃniyokṣyeti" niścitaṃ cittotpādaṃ karoti / asyā api pratijñāyā advayajñānaprahāṇe sādhayitumaśakyatvād, advayajñāne 'pi āvaśyaka eva avatāraḥ, ataḥ sarvabuddhadharmāṇāṃ bījaṃ karuṇā eva asti / yathā ratnāvalyām uktam- karuṇāpūrvakāḥ sarve niṣyandā jñānanirmalāḥ / uktā yatra mahāyāne kastannindet sacetanaḥ //
body.translated_text: Just as for the attainment of external grain and other [crops], the seed, water, and ripening are primary at the beginning, middle, and end respectively, and there is no usefulness [without them], so too the usefulness of compassion alone at all three times for the attainment of the harvest of the <s>Jina</s> is thus taught. Thus, the compassionate one, being pained by the suffering of others, for the protection of all beings who have become entirely immersed in suffering, generates the arising of the mind with firm resolve: 'I shall certainly rescue this entire world from suffering and establish them in Buddhahood.' Since this vow too cannot be accomplished without the elimination through non-dual knowledge, entry into non-dual knowledge is indeed indispensable. Therefore, the seed of all <s>Buddha</s>-qualities is compassion alone. As stated in the <s>Ratnāvalī</s>: 'All the outflows, preceded by compassion, purified by knowledge, are declared in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> — what conscious person would disparage that?'

body.text: bodhicittotpāde 'pi yadi uttarakāle karuṇājalena punaḥ punaḥ na siñcitaḥ asañcitavipulaphalasaṃbhāro 'yam avaśyaṃ śrāvakapratyekabuddhayoḥ parinirvāṇe parinirvṛtto bhaviṣyati / anantaphalāvasthāyāṃ prāptāyāmapi yadi parakāle karuṇā paripākarahitā syād asyāḥ dīrghakālopabhogo na bhaviṣyati, āryaphalamahāsambhāraphalakramaparamparāsvabhāvo 'pi nirantaraṃ dīrghaṃ nābhivardheta / samprati ālambanaviśeṣapraveśadvāreṇapi karuṇāyāḥ svabhāvaviśeṣam abhivyajya tasyai eva praṇāmacikīrṣayā-
body.translated_text: Even after the arising of <s>bodhicitta</s>, if in subsequent times it is not again and again watered with the water of compassion, then, without having accumulated the vast store of merit, this [bodhisattva] will inevitably attain final <s>nirvāṇa</s> in the <s>parinirvāṇa</s> of the <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>. Even when the state of infinite fruit has been reached, if at a later time compassion were to lack full ripening, its long enjoyment would not come about, and even the successive stages of the great accumulation of noble fruits would not continuously grow over a long period. Now, in order to manifest the distinctive nature of compassion through the door of entering into the distinction of its object, and with the desire to pay homage to that very [compassion]:

children.text: ātmābhisaktau tvahameti pūrvaṃ rāgodbhave bhāva idaṃ mameti /
children.translated_text: First, through attachment to self, thinking 'I'; then, through the arising of attachment to things, thinking 'this is mine' —

children.text: arhaṭṭacaryāvadadhīnaloke kāruṇyavān yo 'sti namo 'stu tasmai // Madhy_1.3 //
children.translated_text: like a waterwheel operating on beings who are without self-control — homage to the one who possesses compassion! (Madhyamakāvatāra 1.3)

body.text: ityuktam /
body.translated_text: Thus it is said.

body.text: asya lokasya tu mamābhiniveśāt pūrvam eva ahaṃgrahaṇād ' asantam ātmānam' astīti parikalpya atraiva satyābhiniveśaḥ, 'idaṃ tu mama' iti / ātmagrahaviṣayato bhinne 'śeṣavidhe vastuni abhiniveśo bhavati / ātmātmīyābhiniviṣṭam idaṃ jagat karmakleśabandhananibaddham cakracālakavijñānotkṣepādhīnapraveśaṃ saṃsāramahākūpabhavāgrato gambhīranirbādhāvīciparyantacalanaṃ, svayameva heṣṭhāgāmi, prayatnataḥ kathañcana ākṛṣyamāṇam, ajñānādikleśakarmajanyasaṃkleśatraye 'pi paurvāparyamadhyakrameṇa aniścitaṃ, pratidinaṃ duḥkhaduḥkhatāvipariṇāmaduḥkhatāpravāhād arhaṭṭaghaṭasyāvasthāto nātivartate, yato bodhisattvo duḥkhena duḥkhitam atikaruṇālambanena trātumiccati, ataḥ sarvaprathamaṃ khalu bhagavatī mahākaruṇā praṇamyate / iyaṃ bodhisattvakaruṇā tu sattvālambaneti /
body.translated_text: This world, prior to all else, through attachment to 'mine,' first grasps at 'I' and fabricates 'a self that does not exist' as existing, then develops attachment to the truth of that very [fabrication], thinking 'this is mine.' Attachment arises toward every kind of object distinct from the object of self-grasping. This world, attached to self and what belongs to self, bound by the bonds of <s>karma</s> (action) and <s>kleśa</s> (affliction), with its entry dependent upon the tossing up of consciousness like a waterwheel operator, moving from the front of the great well of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence) down to its deep, unobstructed <s>Avīci</s> (lowest hell) depths, descending by itself, somehow drawn upward only with effort — uncertain even in the sequence of earlier, later, and middle among the three categories of defilement produced by ignorance and other afflictions and <s>karma</s> — does not transcend the condition of a waterwheel bucket, day after day, in the stream of the suffering of suffering (<s>duḥkhaduḥkhatā</s>), the suffering of change (<s>vipariṇāmaduḥkhatā</s>), and [the suffering of conditioned existence]. Because the <s>Bodhisattva</s> wishes to rescue beings pained by suffering through the object of supreme compassion, therefore the blessed <s>mahākaruṇā</s> (great compassion) is first and foremost saluted. This compassion of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is called '<s>sattvālambana</s>' (compassion with sentient beings as its object).

body.text: dharmālambanāṃ nirālambanāṃ ca karuṇāmapi avalambanadvārā prakāśayitum uktam-
body.translated_text: In order to reveal through the door of objects the compassion that has <s>dharmas</s> as its object (<s>dharmālambana</s>) and that is objectless (<s>nirālambana</s>), it is said:

body.text: jagaccale candramivāmbumadhye calaṃ svabhāvena vinā vilokya /
body.translated_text: Seeing the world as moving, like the moon in water, moving and without inherent nature —

body.text: kāruṇyavān yo 'sti namo 'stu tasmai, iti tatra yojitavyam / mandavāyulaghutaraṃgitasvacchajalābhyantaravyāptacandrapratibimbaṃ pūrvāvalambitāśrayaviṣayeṇa saha naśyati, tayorbhāvapratyakṣe avalambatvena udaye sati, uttamaistu etadvayaṃ svabhāvatāprakāśanasadṛśaṃ sthitaṃ dṛśyate- evam pratikṣaṇaṃ anityatāsvabhāvaśūnyatā ca / tathā bodhisattvaiḥ karuṇāparatantrībhūtairapi satkāyadṛṣṭayavidyāsāgare sāgaraśreṣṭhadharmāmṛtarasodbhavahetave sakalaviparītakalpanālakṣaṇe sampūrṇe jagati ayoniśovikalpamārutaprerite nīlavistṛtāvidyājale sthitān prāṇinaḥ svakarmapratibimbavatpuraḥsthitān pratikṣaṇaṃ anityaduḥkhapatītān svabhāvaśūnyān dṛṣṭvā tayoranityatāduḥkhavināśasadṛśabhūtān saddharmaśreṣṭhāmṛtarasodbhavahetave sakalaviparītakalpanānivṛttilakṣaṇaṃ sampūrṇaṃ jagat bandhutvasvabhāvabhūtaṃ buddhatvaṃ samyakprāpayitumiṣyate /
body.translated_text: homage to the one who possesses compassion! — this should be connected there. The reflection of the moon pervading the interior of clear water with gentle ripples stirred by a soft breeze perishes together with its previously apprehended basis and object. When the two [basis and reflection] appear in direct perception as dependent, the wise see these two as resembling the manifestation of their own nature — thus, moment by moment, [there is] impermanence and emptiness of inherent nature. Likewise, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, though fully governed by compassion, in order to produce the nectar of the supreme <s>Dharma</s> of the ocean-like [wisdom] in the ocean of the view of a self-existing group (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) and ignorance — in the complete world characterized by all inverted conceptualizations, agitated by the wind of improper conceptualization, in the vast blue water of ignorance — seeing beings standing there like reflections of their own <s>karma</s>, moment by moment impermanent, fallen into suffering, and empty of inherent nature, resembling the destruction of those [reflections in] impermanence and suffering, they wish to properly lead the complete world, whose nature is that of kinship, to Buddhahood in order to produce the nectar of the supreme true <s>Dharma</s>, characterized by the cessation of all inverted conceptualizations.

body.text: teṣāṃ yā karuṇā sattvālambanā, dharmālambanā anālambanā ca tāṃ praṇamya bodhisattvānāṃ bodhicittasya daśavidhabhedāvivakṣayā saḥ prathamabodhicittam adhikṛtya evaṃ vadati-
body.translated_text: Having paid homage to their compassion — that which has sentient beings as its object, that which has <s>dharmas</s> as its object, and that which is objectless — with the intention of expounding the tenfold division of the <s>Bodhisattva's bodhicitta</s>, he speaks regarding the first <s>bodhicitta</s> thus:

body.text: yadasya citte khalu bodhisattve, jagad vimuktyai karuṇāvaśaṃge // Madhy_1.4 //
body.translated_text: When in the mind of this <s>Bodhisattva</s>, [there arises] for the liberation of the world, under the sway of compassion — (Madhyamakāvatāra 1.4)

body.text: samantabhadrapraṇidhānanāmni, pramoditā sā prathametyavasthataḥ /
body.translated_text: that [mind] named after the vow of <s>Samantabhadra</s>, called '<s>Pramuditā</s>' (Joyful), is established from [this] first stage.

body.text: bodhisattvānām anāsravajñānasya karuṇādibhiḥ parigrahāvibhāgobhūmiriti nāma prāpnoti, guṇāśrayabhūtatvāt tasyā ca uttarottaraṃ guṇasaṃkhyābalātiśayaprāptidānādipāramitāpāṭhaparipākavṛddhiviśeṣeṇa pramuditādibhūmiprakārabhedena daśavidhabhedā vyavasthāpitāḥ, atra svabhāvaviśeṣabhedo na bhavati / yathā- yathāntarīkṣe śakuneḥ padaṃ budhairvaktuṃ na śakyaṃ na ca darśanopagam /
body.translated_text: The stage of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> obtains its name as the indivisible ground of the undefiled knowledge of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> embraced by compassion and other [qualities], because it is the basis of qualities. Through the special distinction of growth in the sequence of the number and power of qualities and the ripening of the practice of the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) such as <s>dāna</s> (generosity) and so forth, progressing ever higher, ten divisions are established in the form of the stages beginning with <s>Pramuditā</s> (Joyful); therein, there is no difference in essential nature. As [it is said]: 'Just as the path of a bird in the sky cannot be stated or perceived by the wise, so too all the stages of the children of the <s>Jina</s> cannot be stated — how much less heard!'

body.text: tathaiva sarvā jinaputrabhūmayo vaktuṃ na śakyāḥ kuta eva śrotum // ityuktam /
body.translated_text: Thus it is said.

body.text: tatra bodhisattvabhūmiḥ pramuditā bodhisattvānāṃ prathamaścittotpādaḥ, antimaśca dharmamegho daśamaścittotpādaḥ / tatra bodhisattvasya yathoktavidhinā- jagat niḥsvabhāvadarśakaṃ karuṇāviśeṣeṇa upagṛhītaṃ yaccitaṃ karuṇāparatantraṃ sat bodhisattvasamantabhadrapraṇidhānena pariṇāmitaṃ pramuditamiti nāmakam, advayajñānaṃ tasya sahetukaṃ phalopalakṣaṇaṃ tatra prathama iti kathyate / daśamahāpraṇidhānādīni daśāsaṃkhyaśatasāhasrapraṇidhānāni, tatra bodhisattvaḥ prathamaṃ cittotpādaṃ karoti, tāni bodhisattvasamantabhadrapraṇidhānamadhye samāhitāni, aśeṣapraṇidhānopasaṃgrahatvāt samantabhadrapraṇidhānaṃ viśeṣeṇa sandṛbdham / tatra yathāśrāvakayāne praveśaphalamārgasthitibhedena aṣṭa śrāvaka bhūmivyavasthā tathā mahāyāne 'pi bodhisattvānāṃ daśabodhisattvabhūmayaḥ / punaśca yathā śrāvakasya nirvedhabhāgīyāvasthotpādaḥ prathamaphalapraveśāvasthā na manyate tathā bhāvināṃ bodhisattvānāmapi / ratnameghasūtre mahādhimuktamahācaryādharmatāyā anantaraṃ prāpteyaṃ prathamabhūmisthitistu bodhisattvasya bodhicittānutpādabhūmirityuktavat / adhimukticaryāyāstatkṣaṇāsthitirapi- 'kulaputra! tadyathā- yathā cakravartī rājā mānuṣavarṇātīto na tu devavarṇaprāptaḥ, tathaiva bodhisattvo 'pi laukikaśrāvakapratyekabuddhānāṃ sarvabhūmyatītaḥ, na tu bodhisattvaparamārthabhūmiprāptaḥ / iti tatraiva vyākhyātam / punaśca yadā iha pramuditākhyaprathamabhūmau praveśaḥ- tataḥ samārabhya tu tatra prāptaḥ sa bodhisattveti padābhidheyaḥ // Madhy_1.5 //
body.translated_text: Therein, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage called <s>Pramuditā</s> (Joyful) is the first arising of the mind of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, and the last, <s>Dharmameghā</s> (Cloud of Dharma), is the tenth arising of the mind. Therein, when the mind of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, as prescribed — seeing the world as without inherent nature, embraced by the special distinction of compassion, that mind governed by compassion, transformed by the vow of <s>Bodhisattva Samantabhadra</s> — is named <s>Pramuditā</s> (Joyful), the non-dual knowledge together with its cause, indicative of the fruit, is called 'the first' there. The ten great vows and so forth, up to one hundred thousand times ten million vows — therein the <s>Bodhisattva</s> generates the first arising of the mind; these are included within the vow of <s>Bodhisattva Samantabhadra</s>; because it encompasses all vows, the vow of <s>Samantabhadra</s> is specifically mentioned. Just as in the <s>śrāvaka</s> vehicle there are eight stages of <s>śrāvakas</s> established according to the distinctions of the path of entry, fruition, and abiding, so too in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> there are ten <s>Bodhisattva</s> stages. Furthermore, just as the arising of the <s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s> (penetrative) stage of the <s>śrāvaka</s> is not considered the stage of first fruition-entry, so too for future <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. In the <s>Ratnameghāsūtra</s>, immediately after the great aspiration and great practice of <s>dharmatā</s>, this first stage-abiding of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is called the stage of the non-arising of <s>bodhicitta</s>. Even the momentary non-abiding of the aspiration practice — 'Son of good family! Just as a wheel-turning king has surpassed the appearance of humans but has not attained the appearance of gods, so too the <s>Bodhisattva</s> has surpassed all worldly stages of <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> but has not attained the ultimate <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage' — is explained there. Furthermore, when there is entry into this first stage called <s>Pramuditā</s>: 'From that point onward, having arrived there, he is designated by the term <s>Bodhisattva</s>.' (Madhyamakāvatāra 1.5)

body.text:
taccittaprāptastu sarvathā pṛthagjanabhūmyatikrāntāvasthāyāṃ bodhisattvapade- naivābhidhīyate, nānyathā, tatsamaye tasya āryabhūtatvāt / yathā- bhagavatyāṃ paṃcaviṃśaśatikāyāṃ- "bodhisattva ityanubuddhasattvasyaitadadhivacanam, yena sarvadharmā buddhā jñātāḥ / kathaṃ jñātāḥ? abhūtā asaṃbhūtā avitathāḥ, naite tathā yathā bālapṛthagjanaiḥ kalpitāḥ / naite tathā yathā bālapṛthagjanairlabdhāḥ / tenocyate bodhisattvā iti / tatkasya hetoḥ? akalpitā avikalpitā hi bodhiḥ, aviṭhapitā hi bodhiḥ, anupalambhā hi bodhiḥ / na hi suvikrāntavikrāmiṃstathāgatena bodhirlabdhā / alambhātsarvadharmāṇāmanupalambhātsarvadharmāṇāṃ bodhirityucyate / evaṃ buddhabodhirityucyate, na punaryathocyate / yena suvikrāntavikrāmin bodhāya cittamutpādayanti idaṃ cittaṃ bodhāyotpādayiṣyāma iti bodhiṃ manyante, astyasau bodhiryasyāṃ vayaṃ cittamutpādayiṣyāma iti, na te bodhisattvā ityucyante, utpannasattvāsta ucyante / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? tathā hi utpādābhiniviṣṭāścittābhiniviṣṭā bodhimabhiniviśante /" ityādi uktam / punaśca- "alakṣaṇā hi bodhirlakṣaṇasvabhāvavinivṛttā / ya evamanubodhaḥ, iyamucyate bodhiriti, na punaryathocyate / eṣāṃ hi suvikrāntavikrāmin dharmāṇāmanubodhatvādvodhisattva ityucyate / yo hi kaścit suvikrāntavikrāmin imān dharmānaprajānannanavabudhyamāno bodhisattva ityātmānaṃ pratijānīte, dūre tasya bodhisattvasya bodhisattvabhūmiḥ, dūre bodhisattvadharmāḥ, visaṃvādayati sadevamānuṣāsuraṃ lokaṃ bodhisattvanāmnā / sacetpunaḥ suvikrāntavikrāmin vāṅmātreṇa bodhisattvo bhavet, tena sarvasattvā api bodhisattvā bhaveyuḥ / naitatsuvikrāntavikrāmin vāṅmātraṃ yaduta bodhisattvabhūmiriti /" ityādi
uktam / yathoktaṃ bodhicittaṃ prāptastu tasyām avasthāyāṃ bodhisattvaśabdadvārā eva kevalaṃ na ukto 'pi tu-
body.translated_text: However, the one who has attained that mind, in the state of having entirely transcended the ground of ordinary beings, is designated by the word '<s>Bodhisattva</s>' alone, and not otherwise, since at that time he has become a Noble One (<s>ārya</s>). As stated in the <s>Pañcaviṃśatisāhasrikā</s> (the Perfection of Wisdom in Twenty-Five Thousand Lines): 'The word <s>Bodhisattva</s> is a designation for one whose being (<s>sattva</s>) is awakened (<s>anubuddha</s>), by whom all <s>dharmas</s> have been awakened to and known. How have they been known? As unborn, unarisen, and not false — not as they are imagined by foolish ordinary beings, not as they are apprehended by foolish ordinary beings. Therefore they are called <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. For what reason? Because <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) is unimagined and unconceptualized; because <s>bodhi</s> is unestablished; because <s>bodhi</s> is unapprehendable. For, O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, <s>bodhi</s> was not obtained by the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Because of the unobtainability of all <s>dharmas</s>, because of the unapprehendability of all <s>dharmas</s>, it is called <s>bodhi</s>. Thus it is called <s>buddhābodhi</s> (Buddha's awakening), but not in the way it is spoken of. O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, those who generate the mind for awakening, thinking "We shall generate this mind for <s>bodhi</s>," and who conceive of <s>bodhi</s>, thinking "There exists that <s>bodhi</s> toward which we shall generate the mind" — they are not called <s>Bodhisattvas</s>; they are called <s>utpannasattvas</s> (beings of arising). For what reason? Because, being attached to arising and attached to mind, they become attached to <s>bodhi</s>.' And so forth, as stated. And further: 'For <s>bodhi</s> is without characteristics, having turned away from the intrinsic nature of characteristics. That which is thus an awakening — this is called <s>bodhi</s>, but not in the way it is spoken of. Because of the awakening to these <s>dharmas</s>, O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, one is called a <s>Bodhisattva</s>. Whoever, O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, not understanding and not awakening to these <s>dharmas</s>, claims himself to be a <s>Bodhisattva</s> — for him the <s>Bodhisattva</s> stages are far away, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> qualities are far away; he deceives the world with its gods, humans, and <s>asuras</s> by the name of <s>Bodhisattva</s>. If, O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, one could become a <s>Bodhisattva</s> by mere words, then all beings would also be <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. This, O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, is not merely words — namely, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage.' And so forth, as stated. However, the one who has attained the <s>bodhicitta</s> as described, in that state, is not designated merely through the word '<s>Bodhisattva</s>' — but moreover:

children.text: gotre 'pi bhāvo 'sya tathāgatānāṃ tyaktaṃ trisaṃyojanamasya sarvam /
children.translated_text: In him there is also the nature of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>' lineage (<s>gotra</s>); all his three fetters (<s>saṃyojana</s>) are abandoned;

children.text: prāmoditāṃ prāpya sa bodhisattvaḥ kṣobdhuṃ samarthaḥ śatalokadhātum // Madhy_1.6 //
children.translated_text: having attained the Joyful (<s>Pramuditā</s>) stage, that <s>Bodhisattva</s> is capable of shaking a hundred world-systems. // Madhyamakāvatāra 1.6 //

body.text: pṛthagjanaśrāvakapratyekabuddhasarvabhūmyatītatvāt samantaprabhetitathāgatabhūmyanugāmimārgotpannatvācca sa bodhisattvaḥ tathāgatagotrotpannaḥ / tadā pudgalanairātmyaṃ pratyakṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā iyaṃ satkāyadṛṣṭisaṃśayaśīlavrataparamārthateti saṃyojanatrayebhyo 'pi sannivartate, teṣāṃ punaranutpādāya / tattvādraṣṭurātmani āropāt satkāyadṛṣṭirbhavati, tathā saṃśayatastasyāparamārge 'pi gamanaṃ saṃbhāvyate, na cānyasya / niścayapraveśe tasya sahetukaguṇaprāptiḥ, bhūmerasapakṣadoṣanivṛtteśca asāmānyaviśeṣamuditotpādād atipramuditāvaśāt sa bodhisattvo 'gramuditām api dhārayati / pramodaviśeṣabhūtatvād iyam bhūmistu pramuditeti nāmāpi prāptā / śatalokadhātuṃ kṣobdhumapi samarthaḥ /
body.translated_text: Because he has transcended all the stages of ordinary beings, <s>śrāvakas</s>, and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, and because the path following the <s>Tathāgata</s> stage called <s>Samantaprabhā</s> (Universally Luminous) has arisen in him, that <s>Bodhisattva</s> is born in the lineage of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>. Then, having directly seen the selflessness of persons (<s>pudgalanairātmya</s>), he turns away from even the three fetters — the view of the perishable collection (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>), doubt (<s>saṃśaya</s>), and clinging to rules and rituals (<s>śīlavrataparāmarśa</s>) — so that they never arise again. The view of the perishable collection arises from superimposition upon the self by one who sees reality; likewise, from doubt, the possibility of his going on a wrong path is entertained, and not of another. Upon entering certainty, he attains qualities together with their causes; and because of the cessation of faults contrary to the stage, due to the uncommon and special arising of joy, by the force of the stage of Supreme Joy (<s>Atipramuditā</s>), that <s>Bodhisattva</s> also bears the name of 'Supremely Joyful.' Because it is the ground of a special delight, this stage has obtained the name <s>Pramuditā</s> (Joyful). He is also capable of shaking a hundred world-systems.

children.text: prayāti bhūmeḥ khalu bhūmimūrdhvaṃ tadāsya mārgo kugaterniruddhaḥ /
children.translated_text: He ascends from stage to stage upward, and then his path to an evil destiny (<s>kugati</s>) is blocked;

children.text: pṛthagjanasyāvanisaṃkṣayo 'sti yathāṣṭamāryaḥ kathitastathaiṣaḥ // Madhy_1.7 //
children.translated_text: the ground of ordinary being is destroyed — just as the eighth Noble One (<s>aṣṭama ārya</s>) is described, so is he. // Madhyamakāvatāra 1.7 //

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text: ayam yathāvabuddhadharmābhyāsād dvitīyabhūmyādyatikramātyutsāhād bhūmerbhūmiṃ samākramya ūrdhvaṃ prayāti / saṃkṣepeṇa yathā srotaāpannāryaḥ svānurūpāryadharmādhigamād doṣarahito guṇānvitaśca bhavati tathā asmin bodhisattve 'pi bhūmyadhigamāt svasmin anurūpaguṇodbhavād doṣakṣayācca strotaāpatterudāharaṇadvārā paridīpitam / ayam bodhisattvastu sambodhicittodaya ādike 'pi pratyekabuddhān samunīndravāgjān /
body.translated_text: This one, through enthusiasm born of practicing the <s>dharmas</s> as they have been understood, ascending from stage to stage beginning with the second, progresses upward. In brief, just as a Noble One who has entered the stream (<s>srotāpanna</s>) becomes free from faults and endowed with qualities through the attainment of noble qualities appropriate to him, so too in this <s>Bodhisattva</s>, through the attainment of stages, the arising of qualities appropriate to himself and the diminution of faults is illustrated by the example of the stream-enterer. Moreover, this <s>Bodhisattva</s>, even at the initial arising of the mind of supreme awakening, surpasses the <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> who are born of the speech of the Lord of sages,

body.text: jittvaidhate puṇyabalena cāpi /
body.translated_text: and he also grows through the power of merit.

body.text: yadasti tadaparo viśeṣaḥ, yathā- āryamaitrīvimokṣa uktam "tadyathā kulaputra acirajāto rājaputro mūrdhaprāptān sarvavṛddhāmātyānabhibhavati kulābhijātyādhipatyena, evameva acirotpāditabodhicittastathāgatadharmarājakulapratyājāta ādikarmiko bodhisattvaściracaritabrahmacaryān vṛddhaśrāvakānabhibhavati bodhicittamahākaruṇādhipatyena /"
body.translated_text: That this is so is a further distinction, as stated in the noble <s>Maitrīvimokṣa</s>: 'For example, <s>Kulaputra</s> (son of good family), a prince just born overcomes all aged ministers established at the summit by the sovereignty of noble birth; even so, a beginner <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has newly generated <s>bodhicitta</s>, reborn in the family of the <s>Tathāgata Dharmarāja</s> (King of <s>Dharma</s>), overcomes the aged <s>śrāvakas</s> who have long practiced the holy life, by the sovereignty of <s>bodhicitta</s> and <s>mahākaruṇā</s> (great compassion).'

body.text: "tadyathā kulaputra, yo 'cirajātasya mahāgaruḍendrapotasya pakṣavātabalaparākramo nayanapariśuddhiguṇaśca, sa sarvaśarīrapravṛddhānāṃ tadanyeṣāṃ pakṣiṇāṃ na saṃvidyate, evameva yaḥ prathamacittotpādikasya tathāgatamahāgaruḍendrasya kulagotrasaṃbhavasya bodhisattvamahāgaruḍendrapotasya sarvajñatācittotpādabalaparākramo mahākaruṇādhyāśayanayanapariśuddhiguṇaśca, sa kalpaśatasahasraniryātānāṃ sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhānāṃ na saṃvidyate /" ityādyuktavat /
body.translated_text: 'For example, <s>Kulaputra</s>, the power and valor of the wing-wind and the quality of visual purity of the young offspring of the great <s>Garuḍa</s>-king, just born, are not found in all other birds with fully grown bodies; even so, the power and valor of the generation of the mind of omniscience and the quality of visual purity of the aspiration of <s>mahākaruṇā</s> (great compassion) of a <s>Bodhisattva</s>-offspring of the great <s>Garuḍa</s>-king who is the <s>Tathāgata</s>, arisen from the family-lineage, who has generated the first <s>cittotpāda</s> (arising of the mind), are not found in all <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> who have trained for hundreds of thousands of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons).' And so forth, as stated.

body.text: dūraṅgamāyāṃ tu dhiyādhikaḥ syāt // Madhy_1.8 //
body.translated_text: But at the Far-Going (<s>Dūraṅgamā</s>) stage, he surpasses [them] in wisdom as well. // Madhyamakāvatāra 1.8 //

body.text: āryadaśabhūmi(sūtre) 'pi- "tadyathāpi nāma bhavanto jinaputrāḥ, rājakulaprasūto rājaputro rājalakṣaṇasamanvāgato jātamātra eva sarvāmātyagaṇamabhibhavati rājādhipatyena, na punaḥ svabuddhivicāreṇa / yadā punaḥ sa saṃvṛddho bhavati tathā svabuddhibalādhānataḥ sarvāmātyakriyāsamatikrānto bhavati, evameva bho jinaputrāḥ, bodhisattvaḥ sahacittotpādena sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhānabhibhavatyadhyāśayamāhātmyena, na punaḥ svabuddhivicāreṇa / asyāṃ tu saptamyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthito bodhisattvaḥ svaviṣayajñānaviśeṣamāhātmyāvasthitatvātsarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhakriyāmatikrānto bhavati" // iti yathoktavat / ata evaṃ sati dūraṃgamata eva ārabhya bodhisattvaḥ sva buddhibalotpādane 'pi śrāvakapratyekabuddhāṃścābhibhavati, na cādhobhūmiṣviti jñeyam / asmādāgamāt sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddheṣvapi sarvadharmaniḥsvabhāvatājñānamapi astīti nirbhāseta / asati ca tathā niḥsvabhāvabhāvaparijñānarahitatvāt laukikavītarāgavat tānapi prathamacittotpādabodhisattvā api svabuddhivicāreṇāpi abhibhavanti / tīrthikavat eteṣāṃ tridhātuṣu caryāyā sarvakleśaprahāṇamapi na bhavati / rūpādīnāṃ svalakṣaṇāvalambanaviparyayāt pudgalanairātmyabodho 'pi na bhavati, ātmaprajñaptihetuskandhāvalambanāt / yathā ratnāvalyām uktam-
body.translated_text: As stated also in the noble <s>Daśabhūmisūtra</s>: 'For example, O sons of the <s>Jina</s>, a prince born in a royal family, endowed with the marks of a king, merely by being born already overcomes the entire assembly of ministers by the sovereignty of kingship, but not yet by his own intellectual discernment. But when he has matured, then by the power of his own intelligence he surpasses all the activities of the ministers. Even so, O sons of the <s>Jina</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, together with the arising of his mind, overcomes all <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> by the greatness of his aspiration, but not yet by his own intellectual discernment. But a <s>Bodhisattva</s> abiding on this seventh <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage, because of being established in the greatness of the special knowledge of his own domain, surpasses all the activities of <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>.' Thus, as stated. Therefore, it being so, from the <s>Dūraṅgamā</s> (Far-Going) stage onward, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> surpasses <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> even in the production of his own intellectual power, but not on the lower stages — this should be understood. From this scriptural authority, it would appear that even among all <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> there exists knowledge of the essencelessness of all <s>dharmas</s> (<s>sarvadharmaniḥsvabhāvatā</s>). But since this is not so — because of the absence of full comprehension of the nature of essencelessness — like those who have attained worldly detachment, even those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> at the initial arising of the mind surpass them even by their own intellectual discernment. Like non-Buddhist ascetics (<s>tīrthikas</s>), even the complete abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (defilements) in the three realms does not occur for them in their practice. Because of the error of apprehending the own-characteristics of form and so forth, the understanding of the selflessness of persons (<s>pudgalanairātmya</s>) also does not arise, since they apprehend the aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>) which are the basis for the designation of a self. As stated in the <s>Ratnāvalī</s>:

children.text: "skandhagrāho yāvadasti tāvadevāhamityapi /
children.translated_text: 'As long as there is grasping at the aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>), so long there is also [the notion] "I";

children.text: ahaṅkāre sati punaḥ karma janma tataḥ punaḥ //
children.translated_text: when there is ego-grasping (<s>ahaṅkāra</s>), there is again <s>karma</s> (action), and from that, birth again.

children.text: trivartmaitadanādyantamadhyaṃ saṃsāramaṇḍalam /
children.translated_text: This threefold path, without beginning, end, or middle, is the wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence);

children.text: alātamaṇḍalaprakhyaṃ bhramatyanyonyahetukam //
children.translated_text: resembling a whirling firebrand, it revolves with mutual causation.

children.text: svaparobhayatastasya traikālye cāpyanāptitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Since that [ego-grasping] is not found in oneself, in another, in both, or in any of the three times,

children.text: ahaṅkāraḥ kṣayaṃ yāti tataḥ karma ca janma ca //
children.translated_text: the ego-grasping (<s>ahaṅkāra</s>) comes to an end, and thereby <s>karma</s> and birth as well.

body.text: "iti //
body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text: api ca-
body.translated_text: And further:

children.text: alātacakraṃ gṛhṇāti yathā cakṣurviparyayāt /
children.translated_text: Just as the eye, through error, apprehends a whirling firebrand as a wheel,

children.text: tathendriyāṇi gṛhṇanti viṣayān sāmpratāniva //
children.translated_text: so too the sense faculties apprehend their objects as if they were present.

children.text: indriyāṇīndriyārthāśca pañcabhūtamayā matāḥ /
children.translated_text: The sense faculties and their objects are considered to be composed of the five elements;

children.text: pratisvaṃ bhūtavaiyarthyādeṣāṃ vyarthatvamarthataḥ //
children.translated_text: since each element is individually meaningless, these [senses and objects] are meaningless in reality.

children.text: nirindhano 'gnirbhūtānāṃ vinirbhāge prasajyate /
children.translated_text: When the elements are analyzed separately, fire without fuel would absurdly follow;

children.text: samparke lakṣaṇābhāvaḥ śeṣeṣvapyeṣa nirṇayaḥ //
children.translated_text: when combined, the absence of characteristics [is the conclusion] — this determination applies to the remaining [elements] as well.

children.text: dvidhāpi bhūtānāṃ vyarthatvātsaṅgatirvṛthā /
children.translated_text: Since the elements are meaningless in both ways, their combination is also futile;

children.text: rthatvātsaṅgateścaivaṃ rūpaṃ vyarthamato 'rthataḥ //
children.translated_text: since the combination is thus meaningless, form is also meaningless in reality.

children.text: vijñānavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskārāṇāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Of consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>), feeling (<s>vedanā</s>), perception (<s>saṃjñā</s>), and formations (<s>saṃskāras</s>) as well — in every respect,

children.text: pratyekamātmavaiyarthyād vaiyarthyaṃ paramārthataḥ //
children.translated_text: since each individually is without self-nature, they are meaningless in the ultimate sense.

children.text: sukhābhimāno duḥkhasya pratīkāre yathārthataḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as the conception of happiness is, in reality, a counteraction of suffering,

children.text: tathā duḥkhābhimāno 'pi sukhasya pratighātajaḥ //
children.translated_text: Likewise, the notion of suffering too arises from the obstruction of pleasure.

children.text: sukhe saṃyogatṛṣṇaivaṃ naiḥsvābhāvyāt prahīyate /
children.translated_text: The craving for union with pleasure is thus abandoned through [seeing its] lack of intrinsic nature,

children.text: duḥkhe viyogatṛṣṇā ca paśyatāṃ muktirityataḥ //
children.translated_text: and the craving for separation from suffering [is also abandoned]; therefore, for those who see this, there is liberation.

children.text: kaḥ paśyatīti ceccitaṃ vyavahāreṇa kathyate /
children.translated_text: If asked 'who sees?'—the mind is spoken of conventionally;

children.text: nahi caittaṃ vinā cittaṃ vyarthatvātra saheṣyate //
children.translated_text: for the mind without mental factors would be purposeless; this is not acceptable here.

children.text: vyarthamevaṃ jaganmatvā yathābhūtyātrirāspadaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having thus understood the world to be purposeless, the sage, abiding in reality,

children.text: nirvāti nirupādāno nirupādānavahnivat // "iti //
children.translated_text: attains <s>nirvāṇa</s> without remainder, like a fire without fuel." Thus it is said.

body.text: bodhisattvaireva tathā niḥsvabhāvatayā dṛṣṭam iti cet, na cāpi tat, śrāvakān pratyekabuddhāṃścādhikṛtya tathoktatvāt / kathamidaṃ jñāyata iti? vakṣyate- samanantarameva bodhisattvān adhikṛtya- "bodhisattvo 'pi dṛṣṭvaivaṃ sambodhau niyato mataḥ / kevalaṃ tvasya kāruṇyādābodherbhavasantatiḥ //"
body.translated_text: If it is objected that <s>Bodhisattvas</s> alone have seen things as lacking intrinsic nature, that is not so either, since it is stated with reference to <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> as well. How is this known? It will be stated—immediately following, with reference to <s>Bodhisattvas</s>: "The <s>Bodhisattva</s> too, having seen thus, is considered firmly established in perfect awakening; but solely because of his compassion, the stream of existence continues until full awakening."

body.text: ityādi uktatvāt / śrāvakadeśanāsūtreṣvapi śrāvakānāṃ kleśāvaraṇaprahāṇārtham- "phenapiṇḍopamaṃ rūpaṃ vedanā budbudopamā / marīcisadṛśī saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ kadalīnibhāḥ / māyopamaṃ ca vijñānamuktamādityabandhunā //"
body.translated_text: And so forth, since it is thus stated. In the <s>sūtras</s> of the <s>śrāvaka</s> teaching as well, for the purpose of the <s>śrāvakas</s>' abandonment of the obscuration of afflictions: "Form is like a mass of foam, feeling is like a water bubble, perception is like a mirage, mental formations are like a plantain trunk, and consciousness is like an illusion—so said the Kinsman of the Sun."

body.text: ityādinā phenapiṇḍajalabudbudamarīcijalakadalīskandhamāyādyudāharaṇena saṃskārā nirṇītā ācāryapādaiḥ- "anutpādo mahāyāne pareṣāṃ śūnyatā kṣayaḥ / kṣayānutpādayoścaikyamarthataḥ kṣamyatāṃ yataḥ //" iti //
body.translated_text: And so forth. Through the examples of a mass of foam, water bubble, mirage, water, plantain trunk, illusion, and so on, the conditioned formations have been ascertained by the venerable master [<s>Nāgārjuna</s>]: "Non-arising in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, emptiness for others, and cessation—let the identity of cessation and non-arising be accepted in meaning, since [they are the same]."

body.text: tathā ca-
body.translated_text: And thus—

children.text: kātyāyanāvavāde cāstīti nāstīti cobhayam /
children.translated_text: In the instruction to <s>Kātyāyana</s>, both 'it exists' and 'it does not exist'

children.text: pratiṣiddhaṃ bhagavatā bhāvābhāvavibhāvinā //
children.translated_text: were prohibited by the <s>Bhagavān</s>, who discerns existence and non-existence.

body.text: śrāvakayāne 'pi dharmanairātmyaṃ deśitamiti tadā mahāyānadeśanā vyarthā syāditi tanmatamapi evaṃ yuktyāgamābhyāṃ viruddhaṃ budhyate / mahāyānadeśanā dharmanairātmyamātrasya deśanā nāsti apitu bodhisattvānāṃ bhūmipāramitāpraṇidhānamahākaruṇādipariṇāmanāsambhāradvaya-acintyadharmatāśca santi / yathā ratnāvalyāmuktam-
body.translated_text: If <s>dharma-nairātmya</s> (selflessness of phenomena) is taught in the <s>śrāvakayāna</s> as well, then the <s>Mahāyāna</s> teaching would be purposeless—this opinion too is understood to be contradicted by both reasoning and scripture. The <s>Mahāyāna</s> teaching is not merely the teaching of <s>dharma-nairātmya</s>; rather, it also contains the <s>bhūmis</s> (stages), <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), vows, great compassion, dedications, the two accumulations, and inconceivable qualities of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. As stated in the <s>Ratnāvalī</s>:

children.text: na bodhisattvapraṇidhirna caryā pariṇāmanā /
children.translated_text: The vow of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, the practice, and the dedication

children.text: uktā śrāvakayāne 'smād bodhisattvaḥ kutastataḥ //
children.translated_text: are not taught in the <s>śrāvakayāna</s>; therefore, from where would a <s>Bodhisattva</s> arise from that?

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus it is said.

children.text: bodhicaryāpratiṣṭhārthaṃ na sūtre bhāṣitaṃ vacaḥ /
children.translated_text: Words not spoken in the <s>sūtras</s> for the purpose of establishing the practice of awakening,

children.text: bhāṣitaṃ ca mahāyāne grāhyamasmād vicakṣaṇaiḥ //
children.translated_text: but spoken in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, should therefore be accepted by the wise.

body.text: dharmanairātmyaprakāśāya mahāyānadeśanāpi yuktā eva, vistṛtadeśanāyā vivakṣitatvāt / śrāvakayāne tu dharmanairātmyaṃ saṃkṣiptalakṣaṇamātreṇa samāpyate / yathā ācāryapādairuktam- animittamanāgamya mokṣo nāsti tvamuktavān / atastvayā mahāyāne tat sākalyena darśitam //
body.translated_text: The <s>Mahāyāna</s> teaching is indeed appropriate for the purpose of illuminating <s>dharma-nairātmya</s>, since an extensive teaching is intended. In the <s>śrāvakayāna</s>, however, <s>dharma-nairātmya</s> is concluded with merely a brief characterization. As the venerable master stated: 'You have said that without resorting to the signless, there is no liberation; therefore, you have shown that completely in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>.'

body.text:
ānuṣaṃgikatvena paryāptam / ata eva anākulabuddheḥ svayamevārthatattvāvabodhasamarthatvāt prakṛtamevābhidhīyate /
tadātra sambuddhasubodhiheturbhavet pradhānaṃ hyatireki dānam /
body.translated_text: This is sufficient as a secondary matter. Therefore, since one of unclouded intellect is capable of understanding the true nature of things by oneself, only the main topic is stated here. Now, for the well-awakened one, the principal cause of perfect awakening that is preeminent is <s>dāna</s> (generosity).

body.text:
tasya pramuditābhūmiprāptabodhisattvasya dānaśīlakṣāntivīryasamādhiprajñā-upāyapraṇidhānabalajñāneṣviti daśasu dānapāramitaiva atiricyate, kintu na tadbhinnānāmabhāvaḥ /
taddānamapi sarvākārajñatāyāḥ pradhāno hetuḥ /
body.translated_text: For that <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has attained the first <s>bhūmi</s> called <s>Pramuditā</s> (Joyful), among the ten [perfections]—<s>dāna</s> (generosity), <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct), <s>kṣānti</s> (patience), <s>vīrya</s> (vigor), <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), <s>upāya</s> (skillful means), <s>praṇidhāna</s> (vows), <s>bala</s> (powers), and <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge)—the perfection of generosity alone is preeminent, though the absence of the others is not implied. That generosity too is the principal cause of <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience in all aspects).

body.text: svamāṃsadāne 'pi kṛtādaratvād bhavedadṛṣṭe 'pyanumānahetuḥ // Madhy_1.9 //
body.translated_text: Because of the reverence shown even in giving one's own flesh, this serves as an inferential reason even for unseen qualities. (Madhyamakāvatāra 1.9)

body.text: tasya bodhisattvasya adṛṣṭā guṇā bodhādayo ye ke 'pi santi te 'pi bāhyābhyantarasvavastudānaviśeṣānumānenaiva sphuṭam anumīyante, dhūmādinā vahnayādivat / yathā bodhisattvānāṃ dānaṃ buddhatvasya pradhānaheturapratyakṣaguṇanirṇayalakṣaṇo 'sti tathā pṛthagjanaśrāvakapratyekabuddhānāmapi duḥkhapratikārasya ātyantikasukhaprāpteśca heturiti deśitukāmena-
body.translated_text: The unseen qualities of that <s>Bodhisattva</s>—awakening and whatever others there may be—are clearly inferred through the inference of the special quality of giving one's own inner and outer possessions, just as fire is inferred from smoke and so forth. Just as the generosity of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> is the principal cause of Buddhahood and serves as the mark for ascertaining imperceptible qualities, so too, wishing to teach that it is the cause of counteracting suffering and attaining ultimate happiness for ordinary beings, <s>śrāvakas</s>, and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> as well—

children.text: sukhābhilāṣī hi janastu sarvaḥ sukhaṃ na sampattimapāsya loke /
children.translated_text: All people indeed desire happiness; happiness in the world cannot [be obtained] by casting away prosperity;

children.text: dhanaṃ tu dānodgatameva buddhvā muniḥ pradhānaṃ samuvāca dānam // Madhy_1.10 //
children.translated_text: knowing that wealth arises from generosity alone, the sage declared generosity to be paramount. (Madhyamakāvatāra 1.10)

body.text: uktam / kṣuttṛḍrogaśītādipratipakṣo duḥkhapratikāramātraṃ, bhavasukhotpādahetupratibandhakaviparyamātreṇa svatvapravāhaparikalpitopaghātāpanayo 'sukhātmake loke 'tīva abhiniviṣṭaḥ tathā tasya sukhābhilāṣiṇaḥ sukhaṃ duḥkhapratikāramātrasvabhāvam, abhīṣṭaviṣayasampattiḥ duḥkhapratipakṣabhūḥ, viparyayātmano bhogaṃ vinā notpādāvalambanam / duḥkhapratikārahetubhūtāste viṣayā api dānodbhūtapuṇyakriyāvastvasaṃcayeṣu notpadyanta iti vicārya bhagavān jagadaśeṣāśayasvabhāvajñaḥ śīlādisamākhyāneṣu sarvaprathamaṃ dānameva āha / adhunā dāniprāṇinaḥ śīlavairūpye 'pi svakāryānukūlatvād dānamāhātmyam ākhyātumāha-
body.translated_text: Thus it is said. The counteracting of hunger, thirst, disease, cold, and so forth is merely the counteraction of suffering. In a world whose nature is unhappiness, one who is deeply attached—through the mere reversal of obstructing causes of worldly happiness—to the removal of the imagined damage to the stream of one's own possessions; for such a seeker of happiness, happiness is merely the counteraction of suffering in nature, the prosperity of desired objects is the ground for counteracting suffering, and without the enjoyment of objects whose nature is the opposite, there is no basis for arising. Having reflected that those sense objects, which serve as causes for counteracting suffering, do not arise without the accumulation of meritorious activity born of generosity, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, who knows the nature of the aspirations of all beings without exception, in the enumeration of moral conduct and other [virtues], spoke of generosity first among all. Now, to proclaim the greatness of generosity, since even for a generous being whose moral conduct is impaired, generosity is favorable to one's own purpose, he says—

children.text: parīttakāruṇyasuduṣṭacittā vikurvate svārthaparā amī ye /
children.translated_text: Those whose compassion is meager, whose minds are thoroughly corrupted, who act out of self-interest—

children.text: tadiṣṭasampad vyasanapraśāntyai samudgatā dānata eva sāpi // Madhy_1.11 //
children.translated_text: even the prosperity they desire, for the cessation of their calamities, arises from generosity alone. (Madhyamakāvatāra 1.11)

body.text: ye vaṇigvat svalpadhanatyāgena ativipulaphalasampatskandhārthecchavo 'pi adhikatarārthārthino ditsādarāḥ, sugataputravat karuṇāparatantrā dānaphalārtham anāyāsameva āditsotsavābhivardhanāste 'pi dānadoṣagrahaṇaparāṅamukhāḥ kevalaguṇagrahaṇotsāhaprāptā atiśayaiśvaryopasampadāḥ kāyāpriyaduḥkhakṣuttṛṣṇādināśanena duḥkhopaśāntiheturbhavanti / yasya niṣkaruṇasya svaduḥkhapratikārāpekṣayā eva ditsāyām ādaraḥ, so 'pi-
body.translated_text: Those who, like merchants, through the sacrifice of small wealth desire the mass of exceedingly abundant fruits and greater prosperity, who are devoted to the intention of giving; those who, like children of the <s>Sugata</s>, are governed by compassion, who for the sake of the fruit of generosity effortlessly increase the celebration of giving—they too, turning away from grasping the faults of generosity, having obtained the enthusiasm of grasping only its virtues, endowed with supreme sovereignty, become the cause of the cessation of suffering through the destruction of bodily discomfort, hunger, thirst, and the like. Even one who is without compassion and whose devotion to giving is only for the sake of counteracting his own suffering—

children.text: kadācidasminnapi dānakāle drutaṃ hi labdhvāryajanābhisaṅgam /
children.translated_text: at some time, even during this occasion of giving, having swiftly obtained the company of noble ones,

children.text: tataḥ samucchidya bhavapravāhaṃ sahetukāṃ śāntimataḥ prayāti // Madhy_1.12 //
children.translated_text: one then cuts off the stream of existence and proceeds from here to peace together with its cause. (Madhyamakāvatāra 1.12)

body.text: ityuktam / dānapatestyāginaḥ samīpe sadbhirgantavyam iti dānādhimuktikā dānakāle āryajanābhisaṃgāt tadupadeśataḥ saṃsāranirguṇatāṃ jñātvā nirmalam āryamārgaṃ sākṣātkurvanti, duḥkhopaśāntyā tyaktāvidyā bhavasantateranādikālataḥ pravṛtāṃ janmamaraṇaparamparāṃ tyaktvā śrāvakapratyekabuddhayānaiḥ parinirvṛtā bhaviṣyanti / ataḥ sāmprataṃ bodhisattvānāṃ dānaṃ bhavanirvāṇasukhaprāptihetuḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus it is said. One should go into the presence of the generous patron—thus, at the time of giving, those with a disposition toward generosity, through the company of noble persons and their instruction, knowing the deficiencies of <s>saṃsāra</s>, directly realize the pure noble path; through the cessation of suffering, having abandoned ignorance, they abandon the succession of births and deaths that has continued from beginningless time, and through the vehicles of <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, they will attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. Therefore, at present, the generosity of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> is the cause of attaining the happiness of both worldly existence and <s>nirvāṇa</s>.

body.text: jagaddhitārthaṃ hi kṛtapratijñāḥ prayānti modaṃ na cireṇa dānaiḥ //
body.translated_text: For those who have made vows for the welfare of the world quickly attain joy through acts of generosity.

body.text: abodhisattvāstu dānasamakālaṃ yathoktadānaphalaṃ niyataṃ na saṃbhuñjanti, tasmād dānaphalasya apratyakṣatvād dāne praveśo 'pi na saṃbhavaḥ, bodhisattvāstu dānasamakālameva arthināmapi paritarpaṇād, abhīṣṭadānaphalasaṃpatparamānandaṃ dhārayantaḥ, tatraiva dānaphalam upabhuñjanti / ataḥ sarvadā dāne muditā bhaviṣyanti / ato yathoktarītyā-
body.translated_text: Non-<s>Bodhisattvas</s>, however, do not necessarily enjoy the stated fruits of generosity at the very time of giving; therefore, since the fruit of generosity is not directly perceptible, entry into generosity may not even occur. But <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, at the very time of giving, through satisfying those who are in need, holding the supreme bliss of the prosperity of desired fruits of giving, enjoy the fruit of generosity right then and there. Therefore, they will always be joyful in giving. Thus, in the manner stated—

body.text: dayādayā bhāvamayā yataśca /
body.translated_text: Since compassion, kindness, and a mind filled with benevolence—

body.text: sarvābhyudayaniḥ śreyasaheturdānam, tato 'sti mūlaṃ khalu dānavārtā // Madhy_1.13 //
body.translated_text: generosity is the cause of all worldly prosperity and ultimate liberation; therefore the practice of generosity is indeed the root. (Madhyamakāvatāra 1.13)

body.text:
yataste sarvadā dānaṃ prati ādareṇa sampadvibhājanadvārā ca manastarpayanti /
bodhisattveṣu ānandaviśeṣotpādaḥ kīdṛśa iti arthināṃ cet- ucyate-
body.translated_text: Since they always satisfy their minds through the gate of distributing their wealth with reverence toward generosity. If asked what kind of special joy arises in <s>Bodhisattvas</s> toward those in need—it is said:

children.text: yathā tu dehīti niśamya śabdaṃ sukhodbhavo buddhasute vicintya /
children.translated_text: Just as, upon hearing the word 'give,' a surge of joy arises in the child of the <s>Buddha</s> upon reflection,

children.text: tathā sukhaṃ śāntigate munau na kimucyatāṃ sarvasamarpaṇeni // Madhy_1.14 //
children.translated_text: such joy does not exist even in a sage who has attained peace—what then need be said of the joy from offering everything? (Madhyamakāvatāra 1.14)

body.text: yāvadarthināṃ dehīti śabdaśrutāveva vicāryamāṇe bodhisattvānām 'ime māṃ yācanta iti buddhavā vāramvāraṃ yaḥ sukhotpādo nirvāṇasukhādapi atiricyate, tato bāhyābhyantaravastusamarpaṇena arthinajanatarpaṇasya kimucyatām? punaḥ kim tat tathoktabāhyābhyantaravastutyāgināṃ bodhisattvānāṃ kāyaduḥkhamapi na bhaviṣyatīti? ucyate- mahātmanāṃ tu acetanānāmapacchedavat kāyaduḥkhotpādo 'sambhava eva /
body.translated_text: When upon merely hearing the word 'give' from those in need, upon reflection, the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> think 'they are asking me,' and the joy that arises again and again surpasses even the bliss of <s>nirvāṇa</s>—then what need be said of the satisfaction of those in need through the offering of inner and outer possessions? Furthermore, will those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who give away their inner and outer possessions as described not experience even bodily suffering? It is said: For great-souled ones, the arising of bodily suffering is impossible, just as the cutting of insentient things [causes no pain].

body.text: āryagaganagañjaparipṛcchāsamādhau yathoktam-
body.translated_text: As stated in the <s>Samādhi</s> of the <s>Āryagaganagañjaparipṛcchā</s> (Noble Gaganagañja's Questions)—

body.text: "tadyathā mahāsālavṛkṣavanamasti / tatra kaścidāgatya ekaṃ saralaṃ chinatti / tatrāvaśiṣṭāste sālavṛkṣā ayaṃ tu chinno, vayaṃ na chinnā iti na cintayanti / teṣu nānurāgo na vā kopaḥ, na kalpo na vikalpaḥ, tadvat bodhisattvasya yā kṣāntiḥ sā pariśuddhāgragaganopametyuktivat /
body.translated_text: "It is like a great forest of <s>sāla</s> trees. There, someone comes and cuts down one <s>sarala</s> (pine) tree. The remaining <s>sāla</s> trees do not think, 'This one is cut, but we are not cut.' There is no attachment toward them nor anger, no conceptualization nor discrimination. Likewise, the <s>kṣānti</s> (patience) of the <s>bodhisattva</s> is said to be like the supremely pure sky."

body.text:
ratnāvalyāmapi evamuktam-
śārīraṃ nāsti vai duḥkhaṃ tatra duḥkhaṃ kva mānasam / loko hi duḥkhitastena karuṇyāt sthīyate ciram // punaryo 'labdhavirāgāvasthastatra kāyasthitibādhakaviṣaye samavatīrṇe kāyaduḥkhaṃ niścitam utpadyate, tadā so 'pi sattvārthakṛtyeṣu ativiśiṣṭāvatārahetutvena pratiṣṭhata iti ākhyātam /
body.translated_text: In the <s>Ratnāvalī</s> also it is said thus: "There is indeed no physical suffering; so where is mental suffering there? The world suffers from that, therefore out of compassion one remains for a long time." Furthermore, when one who has not yet attained the state of dispassion encounters conditions that obstruct physical well-being, bodily suffering certainly arises; at that time, it is declared that this too becomes a cause for extraordinarily distinguished engagement in activities for the benefit of beings.

children.text: pradāya chettuṃ svavapuḥ svaduḥkhāt svasaṃvidā nārakaduḥkhakādi /
children.translated_text: Having given his own body to be cut, from his own suffering, by his own awareness, seeing the sufferings of hell and the like of others,

children.text: vilokya tannāśayituṃ pareṣāṃ pariśramaṃ prārabhate sa śīghram // Madhy_1.15 //
children.translated_text: he quickly begins effort to destroy that suffering of others. || Madhy_1.15 ||

body.text: bodhisattvastu duḥkhamayanarakatiryagyoniyamalokādighoralokāntargataṃ nirantaraghoraduḥkhena kāyacchedaṃ, svakāyacchedaduḥkhāt sahastraśo 'pyadhikaṃ pravṛddhamasahyaṃ duḥkhaṃ svaduḥkhena tulayitvā paśyati tadā svakāyacchedaduḥkhamavigaṇayya sattvānāṃ narakādiduḥkhacchedāya atiśīghraṃ vīryamārabhate / yathoktadānapāramitāprabhedadeśanārtham uktam-
body.translated_text: But the <s>bodhisattva</s>, having compared by his own suffering the unbearable suffering that has increased a thousandfold beyond his own bodily pain — the constant terrible suffering of bodily destruction within the terrible realms of hell, animal births, the world of <s>Yama</s>, and the like, which are full of suffering — seeing this, disregarding the suffering of his own bodily destruction, he quickly begins effort to cut the suffering of hells and the like for beings. For the purpose of teaching the classification of the <s>dāna-pāramitā</s> (perfection of giving) as stated, it is said:

body.text: pradeyasaṅgrāhakadātṛśūnyaṃ vadanti lokottarapāramīti / tatra pāramīti tu yat saṃsārasāgarapāraṃ taṭaṃ, kleśajñeyāvaraṇaniḥśeṣatyāgasvabhāvayukto buddha eva vā / pāraṃgatastu pāramita ityuktam / aluguttarapade ityanena lakṣaṇena karmavibhaktilopaṃ na kṛtvā rūpaṇam, athavā pṛṣodarāditvād uttarapadayuktatayā vyavasthāpitam / prajñāṃ gṛhītvā viśeṣeṇa vyākhyātam, dānādayaḥ pāramitātulyatvāt pāramitāḥ santi / pariṇāmanāviśeṣeṇa pāragamanaṃ vyavasthāpya dānaṃ pāramitānāma prāpnot / vakṣyamāṇāḥ śīlādayo 'pi tathā vijñeyāḥ / iyaṃ dānapāramitāpi deyaṃ, pratigrāhakaṃ dāyakaṃ ca anālambya lokottarapāramitā astīti bhagavatīprajñāpāramitāyām uktam / anālambanasya lokottaratvād ālambanaṃ ca vyavahārasatyasaṃgrahatvāllaukikameva asti / tattu aprāptabodhisattvāvasthābhirjñātuṃ na śakyate / api ca-
body.translated_text: "They call it the supramundane <s>pāramitā</s> when empty of gift, recipient, and giver." There, <s>pāramitā</s> means the other shore of the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>, or indeed the <s>Buddha</s> himself, who is endowed with the nature of complete abandonment of the obstructions of <s>kleśa</s> (affliction) and <s>jñeya</s> (knowledge). 'Gone to the other shore' is called <s>pāramitā</s>. By the characteristic of being an indeclinable superior term, the form is produced without applying case-ending deletion; or else it is established as connected with the latter term through the <s>pṛṣodarādi</s> rule. Taking <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) specifically, it is explained: giving and the others are <s>pāramitās</s> because of being equal to the <s>pāramitā</s>. Having established 'going to the other shore' through the non-distinction of dedication, giving obtains the name <s>pāramitā</s>. The forthcoming <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct) and the others should also be understood in the same way. This <s>dāna-pāramitā</s> too, without clinging to the gift, the recipient, and the giver, is the supramundane <s>pāramitā</s>, as stated in the <s>Bhagavatī-prajñāpāramitā</s>. Because non-clinging is supramundane, and clinging, being included in conventional truth, is indeed mundane. But that cannot be known by those in the stages of <s>bodhisattvas</s> who have not yet attained realization. Moreover —

body.text: trayīṣu rāgodbhavataḥ pradiṣṭaṃ tadeva vai laukikapāramīti // Madhy_1.16 //
body.translated_text: In the three [gift, recipient, giver], arising from attachment, that very same is declared as the mundane <s>pāramitā</s>. || Madhy_1.16 ||

body.text: tadeva dānaṃ triṣvavalambitaṃ sat laukikapāramitetyuktam / samprati yathokta- bhūmiriti jñānaviśeṣeṇa atiśayaguṇānuvādadvārā deśanārthamevamuktam-
body.translated_text: That very giving, when dependent on the three, is called the mundane <s>pāramitā</s>. Now, as stated — the term '<s>bhūmi</s>' (stage) is used for the purpose of teaching through the door of describing extraordinary qualities distinguished by special knowledge — thus it is said:

children.text: tathā pratiṣṭhā jinaputracitte sadāśraye suprabhakāntimāptā /
children.translated_text: Thus established in the mind of the <s>jinaputra</s> (son of the Conqueror), as an ever-present foundation, having attained beautiful and lovely brilliance,

children.text: ghanaṃ tamisraṃ muditā nirasya jayatyasau candramaṇiryathā vai // Madhy_1.17 //
children.translated_text: <s>Muditā</s> (Joy) conquers the dense darkness, just as a moonstone does indeed. || Madhy_1.17 ||

body.text: tathā śabdo yathoktaprakāradeśanārthaḥ / muditeti bhūmināma samākhyāyate / jayatīti tu asapakṣaṃ parājitya avasthānam ityarthaḥ / sā tu jñānasvabhāvā satī eva jinaputramanasi sthitatvād uparisthitā / pramuditābhūmistu yathoktarītyā sarvamapi gahanam andhakāraṃ nirākṛtya jayati / yathokta eva artha udāharaṇena prakāśayitum ākhyātam / candrakāntamaṇivad iti /
body.translated_text: The word 'thus' is for the purpose of teaching in the manner stated. '<s>Muditā</s>' (Joy) is declared as the name of the <s>bhūmi</s> (stage). 'Conquers' means abiding after having defeated opponents. Being of the nature of knowledge, it is established above, abiding in the mind of the <s>jinaputra</s>. The <s>Pramuditā bhūmi</s> (Stage of Joy), in the manner stated, conquers by dispelling all the dense darkness. To illustrate the very meaning stated by an example, it is said: 'like a moonstone.'

body.text:
madhyamakāvatārabhāṣye pramuditeti prathamaścittotpādaḥ /
bodhisattvaprathamacittotpādo vyākhyātaḥ /
body.translated_text: In the <s>Madhyamakāvatāra-bhāṣya</s>: '<s>Pramuditā</s>' is the first generation of <s>citta</s> (mind). The first generation of the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s mind has been explained.

body.text: 2. dvitīyaścittotpādaḥ
body.translated_text: 2. The Second Generation of Mind

body.text: adhunā dvitīyaṃ (cittotpādam) adhikṛtyocyate-
body.translated_text: Now, regarding the second generation of mind, it is said —

body.text: sa śīlasampattiguṇānvitattvāt svapne 'pi duḥśīlamalaṃ jahāti / iti /
body.translated_text: "Due to being endowed with the qualities of perfection of <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct), even in dreams he abandons the stain of immorality."

body.text: bhūmisaṃjñakasarvajñānaviśeṣasya tu ekasvabhāvatvāt tadasatve 'nutpannaguṇabhyaḥ śīlapāramitādiviśiṣṭatābhya eva dvitīyacittotpādādiviśeṣāḥ darśitāḥ / tatra kleśānadhivāsitvāt, pāpānudbhūtatvāt, cittakaukṛtyagniśamanena, śītalatvāt, sukhahetutvena uttamairāśrayaṇīyatvāt śīlamiti / tadapi saptatyāgalakṣaṇam / trayo dharmā alobho 'dveṣaḥ samyagdṛṣṭiśca te samutthānam / ataḥ samutthānena saha śīlam adhikṛtya daśakarmamārgā vyākhyātāḥ śīlasaṃpat tu śīlātiśayaḥ / guṇaviśuddhistu guṇaśuddhiḥ, śīlasaṃpatpariśuddhiriti śabdaḥ prayojyaḥ / svaguṇapariśuddhatvāt śīlatvaṃ viśiṣṭim / tadanvitatvāt sa bodhisattvaḥ svapnāvasthāyāmapi duḥśīlamalairaliptaḥ / atha kathaṃ tasya tādṛk śīlasampadā guṇapariśuddhiḥ? etādṛśo 'yaṃ bodhisattvo dvitīyabodhisattvabhūmau prasthitastu-
body.translated_text: Since the specific knowledge designated as <s>bhūmi</s> (stage) is of one nature, when it is absent, the distinctions of the second generation of mind and so forth are shown through the very excellences of <s>śīla-pāramitā</s> (perfection of moral conduct) and the like, from the qualities not yet arisen. There, because of not harboring <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), because <s>pāpa</s> (sin) does not arise, because of the cooling down of the fire of mental remorse, because of coolness, and because of being the most excellent refuge as a cause of happiness — this is called <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct). That too has seven characteristics of abandonment. Three <s>dharmas</s> — non-greed, non-hatred, and right view — are its basis. Therefore, along with its basis, the ten <s>karmapaths</s> (paths of action) are explained with reference to <s>śīla</s>. Perfection of <s>śīla</s> means the excellence of moral conduct. Purification of qualities means the purity of qualities; the term 'purification of the perfection of <s>śīla</s>' should be used. Due to the purification of his own qualities, moral conduct becomes distinguished. Due to being endowed with that, this <s>bodhisattva</s>, even in the state of dreaming, is untouched by the stains of immorality. Now, how does his perfection of <s>śīla</s> have such purification of qualities? Such a <s>bodhisattva</s>, having set forth on the second <s>bodhisattva-bhūmi</s> —

body.text: sa kāyavākcittaviśuddhacaryo daśaiva satkarmapathāṃścinoti // Madhy_2.1 //
body.translated_text: He, with pure conduct of body, speech, and mind, accumulates the ten wholesome <s>karmapaths</s> (paths of action) alone. || Madhy_2.1 ||

body.text: yathā dvitiyabodhisattvabhūmau- "tatrabhavanto jinaputrā, vimalāyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthito bodhisattvaḥ prakṛtyaiva prāṇātipātātprativirīto bhavati nihatadaṇḍo nihataśastro nihatavairo lajjāvān dayāpannaḥ sarvaprāṇibhūteṣu hitasukhānukampī maitracittaḥ / sa saṃkalpairapi prāṇivihiṃsāṃ na karoti, kaḥ punarvādaḥ parasattveṣu sattvasaṃjñinaḥ saṃcintyaudārikakāyaviheṭhanayā //
body.translated_text: As stated regarding the second <s>bodhisattva-bhūmi</s>: "Here, noble sons of the <s>Jina</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> established on the <s>Vimalā</s> (Stainless) <s>bodhisattva-bhūmi</s> is by nature turned away from killing living beings — with weapons laid down, arms laid down, enmity laid down, possessed of shame, endowed with compassion, thinking of benefit and happiness for all living beings, with a mind of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness). He does not harm living beings even in thought — what need to mention deliberate, gross physical harm to other beings?

body.text: adattādānātprativirataḥ khalu punarbhavati svabhogasaṃtuṣṭaḥ, parabhogānabhilāṣī, anukampakaḥ / sa paraparigṛhītebhyo vastubhyaḥ paraparigṛhītasaṃjñī steyacittamupasthāpya antaśastṛṇaparṇamapi nādattamādātā bhavati, kaḥ punarvādo 'nyebhyo jīvitopakaraṇebhyaḥ //
body.translated_text: "He is indeed turned away from taking what is not given — content with his own possessions, not desiring another's enjoyments, compassionate. Regarding things possessed by others, perceiving them as belonging to others, he does not take even a blade of grass or a leaf with a mind of theft — what need to mention other necessities of life?

body.text: kāmamithyācārātprativirataḥ khalu punarbhavati svadārasaṃtuṣṭaḥ paradārānabhilāṣī / sa paraparigṛhītāsu strīṣu parabhāryāsu gotradhvajadharmarakṣitāsu abhidhyāmapi notpādayati, kaḥ punarvādo dvīndriyasamāpatyā vā anaṅgavijñaptyā vā //
body.translated_text: "He is indeed turned away from sexual misconduct — content with his own wife, not desiring another's wife. He does not generate even covetous thoughts toward women protected by others, wives of others, or those protected by family, custom, and <s>dharma</s> — what need to mention union of the two organs or other bodily intimacy?

body.text: anṛtavacanātprativirataḥ khalu punarbhavati satyavādī, bhūtavādī, kālavādī, yathāvādī tathākārī / so 'ntaśaḥ svapnāntaragato 'pi vinidhāya dṛṣṭiṃ kṣāntiṃ ruciṃ matiṃ prekṣāṃ visaṃvādanābhiprāyo nānṛtāṃ vācaṃ niścārayati, kaḥ punarvādaḥ samanvāhṛtya //
body.translated_text: "He is indeed turned away from false speech — he speaks the truth, speaks what is real, speaks at the right time, practices what he says. Even when he has entered the state of dreaming, having set aside views, convictions, inclinations, opinions, and considerations, he does not utter a false word with the intention of deceiving — what need to mention deliberate falsehood?

body.text: piśunavacanātprativirataḥ khalu punarbhavati abhedāviheṭhāpratipannaḥ sattvānām / sa netaḥ śrutvā amutrākhyātā bhavatyamīṣāṃ bhedāya / na amutaḥ śrutvā ihākhyātā bhavatyeṣāṃ bhedāya / na saṃhitān bhinatti, na bhinnānāmanupradānaṃ karoti / na vyagrārāmo bhavati na vyagrarato na vyagrakaraṇīṃ vācaṃ bhāṣate sadbhūtāmasadbhūtāṃ vā //
body.translated_text: "He is indeed turned away from divisive speech — he is disposed toward non-division and non-harming of beings. Having heard from here, he does not go there to tell for the purpose of dividing those; having heard from there, he does not come here to tell for the purpose of dividing these. He does not break up the united, nor does he encourage those already divided. He does not delight in discord, does not take pleasure in discord, does not speak words that create discord, whether true or false.
