body.text: paruṣavacanātprativirataḥ khalu punarbhavati / sa yeyaṃ vāgadeśā karkaśā parakaṭukā parābhisaṃjananī anvakṣānvakṣaprāgbhārā grāmyā pārthagjanakī anelā akarṇasukhā krodharoṣaniścāritā hṛdayaparidahanī manaḥsaṃtāpakarī apriyā amanaāpā amanojñā svasaṃtānaparasaṃtānavināśinī, tathārūpāṃ vācaṃ prahāya yeyaṃ vāk snigdhā mṛdvī manojñā madhurā priyakaraṇī manaāpakaraṇī hitakaraṇī nelā karṇasukhā hṛdayaṃgamā premaṇīyā paurī varṇavispaṣṭā vijñeyā śravaṇīyā niśritā bahujaneṣṭā bahujanakāntā bahujanapriyā bahujanamanaāpā vijñāpannā sarvasattvahitasukhāvahā samāhitā manaḥ prahlādanakarī svasaṃtānaparasaṃtānaprasādanakarī tathārūpāṃ vācaṃ niścārayati //
body.translated_text: "He is indeed turned away from harsh speech. That speech which is unpleasant, rough, bitter to others, generating hostility, bearing the weight of repeated aggression, vulgar, common, graceless, unpleasant to the ear, uttered from anger and wrath, burning the heart, causing mental anguish, disagreeable, displeasing, unlovely, destroying one's own and others' continuity — having abandoned such speech, that speech which is smooth, gentle, lovely, sweet, pleasing, agreeable, beneficial, graceful, pleasant to the ear, touching the heart, worthy of love, urbane, clear in expression, intelligible, worth hearing, trustworthy, desired by many, loved by many, liked by many, pleasing to many, informative, bringing benefit and happiness to all beings, composed, gladdening the mind, purifying one's own and others' continuity — such speech he utters."

body.text: saṃbhinnapralāpātprativirataḥ khalu punarbhavati suparihāryavacanaḥ kālavādī bhūtavādī arthavādī dharmavādī nyāyavādī vinayavādī, sa nidānavatīṃ vācaṃ bhāṣate kālena sāvadānām / sa cāntaśa itihāsapūrvakamapi vacanaṃ parihāryaṃ pariharati, kaḥ punarvādo vāgvikṣepeṇa //
body.translated_text: One who has ceased from confused, incoherent speech (<s>saṃbhinnapralāpa</s>) speaks agreeably, at the right time, truthfully, meaningfully — speaks of <s>Dharma</s>, speaks according to reason, speaks in accordance with <s>Vinaya</s> (discipline). He speaks purposeful speech, carefully timed. He avoids even speech preceded by stories (<s>itihāsa</s>), how much more so empty prattle.

body.text: anabhidhyāluḥ khalu punarbhavati parasveṣu parakāmeṣu parabhogeṣu paravittopakaraṇeṣu paraparigṛhīteṣu spṛhāmapi notpādayati, kimitiyatpareṣāṃ tannāma syāditi nābhidhyāmutpādayati, na prārthayate, na praṇidadhāti, na lobhacittamutpādayati //
body.translated_text: He is free from covetousness (<s>anabhidhyālu</s>) — he does not generate even desire regarding others' property, others' pleasures, others' enjoyments, others' wealth and possessions, and things possessed by others. The thought 'May this of theirs become mine' — he does not generate such covetousness, does not wish for it, does not set his mind upon it, does not produce a mind of greed.

body.text: avyāpannacittaḥ khalu punarbhavati sarvasattveṣu maitracitto hitacitto dayācittaḥ sukhacittaḥ snigdhacittaḥ sarvajagadanugrahacittaḥ sarvabhūtahitānukampācittaḥ / sa yānīmāni krodhopanāhakhilāmalavyāpādaparidāhasaṃdhukṣitapratighādyāni tāni prahāya yānīmāni hitopasaṃhitāni maitryupasaṃhitāni sarvasattvahitasukhāya vitarkitavicāritāni, tānyanuvitarkayitā bhavati //
body.translated_text: He has an uncorrupted mind (<s>avyāpannacittaḥ</s>) — a mind of loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>) toward all beings, a mind of benefit, a mind of compassion (<s>dayā</s>), a mind of happiness, a mind of affection, a mind of grace toward all the world, a mind of compassionate concern for the welfare of all beings. Those [states] kindled by anger, resentment, malice, hostility, spite, and aggression — having abandoned those, he contemplates thoughts conducive to benefit and loving-kindness, directed toward the happiness and welfare of all beings.

body.text: samyagdṛṣṭiḥ khalu punarbhavati samyakpathagataḥ kautukamaṅgalanānāprakārakuśīladṛṣṭivigata ṛjudṛṣṭiraśaṭho 'māyāvī buddhadharmasaṃghaniyatāśayaḥ / " ityādyuktavat /
body.translated_text: He has right view (<s>samyagdṛṣṭi</s>) — one who has entered the right path, free from various views involving superstition, omens, and improper practices; of straightforward view, without deceit, without guile, with a mind fixed upon the <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Saṅgha</s>. Thus and so forth has been stated.

body.text: tatra prathamatrayakuśalakarmapathāḥ kāyena pratipādyante / madhyamacaturo vācā antyatrayaścittena / evaṃ daśakuśalakarmamārgā api saṃgṛhītāḥ / kim eteṣāṃ karmamārgāṇāṃ cayanaṃ prathamacittotpādabodhisattvā na kurvanti? te 'pi cayanaṃ kurvanti, tathāpi-
body.translated_text: Therein, the first three wholesome karmic paths are practiced by body, the middle four by speech, and the last three by mind. Thus the ten wholesome karmic paths (<s>daśakuśalakarmamārga</s>) are also included. Do first-stage <s>Bodhisattvas</s> (<s>prathamacittotpādabodhisattva</s>) not cultivate these karmic paths? They also cultivate them; nevertheless —

children.text: daśāpi mārgān kuśalān sametya bhavanti te śuddhatarāstathaiva /
children.translated_text: Having gathered all ten wholesome paths, they become purer still in that very way.

children.text: prathamacittotpādabodhisattvā na tathā /
children.translated_text: First-stage <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are not like that [i.e., not yet supremely pure].

children.text: sadā viśuddhaḥ khalu śāradenduryathā hi śāntaprabhayātiśete // Madhy_2.2 //
children.translated_text: Just as the autumn moon is always pure and surpasses with its peaceful radiance — // Madhy 2.2 //

body.text:
śāntastu saṃvṛtendriyaḥ /
prabhāmayo dedīpyamānaśarīraḥ, tathā pariśuddhaśīlaḥ sannapi /
sa śuddhaśīlaprakṛtiṃvidaśced bhavenna tenaiva viśuddhaśīlaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'Peaceful' means 'with restrained senses.' 'Radiant' means 'of a shining body.' Similarly, though his moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>) is pure — 'He who knows the nature of pure moral conduct — yet it is not merely by that that moral conduct is truly purified.'

body.text: yathā-āryaratnakūṭasūtre- "kāśyapa, e[ka]tyo bhikṣuḥ (śīlavantaḥ) prātimokṣasaṃvarasaṃvṛto viharati / ācāragocarasampanna aṇumātreṣvavadyeṣu (api) bhayadarśī samā[dā] ya śikṣate śikṣāpadeṣu pariśuddhakāyakarmavāṅmanaskarmaṇā samanvāgato viharati, pariśuddhājīvaḥ sa ca bha[vati] ātmavādī, ayaṃ kāśyapa prathamo duḥśīlaḥ śīlavaṃtaḥ pratirūpako draṣṭavyaḥ /" ityataḥ "punaraparaṃ kāśyapa! ihe katyo bhikṣuḥ dvādaśādhūtaguṇasa[mādāne 'pi] upalambhadṛṣṭikaśca bhavati, ahaṃkāra(mamakāra)sthitaḥ ayaṃ kāśyapa caturtho duḥśīlaḥ śīlavantapratirūpakodra[ṣṭavyaḥ]" iti paryantam uktam /
body.translated_text: As stated in the <s>Āryaratnakūṭasūtra</s>: '<s>Kāśyapa</s>, a certain monk who is moral dwells restrained by the <s>Prātimokṣa</s> code. He is endowed with proper conduct and range of conduct, sees danger even in the slightest faults, undertakes training in the training rules, dwells endowed with pure bodily action, verbal action, and mental action, and has pure livelihood. Yet he holds a doctrine of self (<s>ātmavādī</s>). This, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is the first type of one who is immoral though appearing moral.' Continuing thus: 'Furthermore, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, a certain monk who upholds even the twelve austere practices (<s>dhūtaguṇa</s>), yet holds a view of apprehension (<s>upalambhadṛṣṭi</s>) and is established in self-grasping (<s>ahaṃkāra</s>) and possessiveness (<s>mamakāra</s>) — this, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is the fourth type of one who is immoral though appearing moral' — thus it is stated to the end.

body.text: ataḥ sadā sastritaye 'pi buddhidvayapracārāt sutarāṃ nivṛttaḥ // Madhy_2.3 //
body.translated_text: Therefore, always, even in the [first] three [wholesome paths], because of the operation of the dual understanding, he is especially free [from attachment]. // Madhy 2.3 //

body.text: kasmai prāṇine tyāgaḥ, kiṃ tyaktaṃ, kena tyaktaṃ, tattritaye 'pi bhāvābhāvādibuddhidvayanirvṛto bhavati / evaṃ saṃprati bodhisattvasya śīlasaṃpanmayatvam uktam / tataḥ paścāt sāmānyatayā tadbhinnānāmapi śīlasampatterdānādito 'pi atiśayatvaṃ sarvaguṇasampadāśrayabhūtatvameva deśanārthayitum uktam-
body.translated_text: To what being is the giving made? What is given? By whom is it given? — regarding this triad too, he is free from the dual understanding of existence and non-existence and so forth. Thus the possession of moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>) by the <s>Bodhisattva</s> has now been explained. Next, in order to teach that even for the divisions of moral perfection, generosity (<s>dāna</s>) and other virtues have surpassing excellence with moral conduct as the ground of all qualities, it is said —

body.text: dānājjanaḥ śīlapadena hīno bhogānavāpyaiṣyati durgatiñca / iti /
body.translated_text: By generosity (<s>dāna</s>) alone, a person lacking the foundation of moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>) will attain [worldly] enjoyments but will proceed to a bad destiny (<s>durgati</s>).

body.text: taddānata eva sa dānapatiḥ śīlavān bhūto naradevamadhye viśiṣṭabhogasampanmayaḥ san śīlapādanirvṛttau durgatilokapatitaḥ pratyekanarakaṃ, aśvagajavānaranāgādipretamaharddhikādiṣu utpannaḥ sa vividhabhogasampatsampanna eva bhavati / ataḥ
body.translated_text: That very patron of giving (<s>dānapati</s>), having become moral, among gods and men, endowed with excellent enjoyments — yet when the foundation of moral conduct fails, having fallen into the worlds of bad destiny, reborn in individual hells, as a horse, elephant, monkey, <s>nāga</s>, or a <s>preta</s> (hungry ghost) of great supernatural power, he is still endowed with various enjoyments. Therefore —

body.text: savyājamūle parikṣīyamāṇe tasmai na bhogāḥ prabhavanti paścāt // Madhy_2.4 //
body.translated_text: When the root of what has been gained, together with its productive capacity, is exhausted, enjoyments do not arise for him afterward. // Madhy 2.4 //

body.text: yo 'tyalpabījamuptvā vipulaphalaṃ prāpnuvan punaḥ phalāya tasmādapyadhikaṃ bījaṃ vapati, tena mahāphalasambhārasya yathāsamaye upavardhanakramo 'vicchinnaṃ sambhavati, kṛtapraṇāśasvabhāvaścayo mūrkhatayā pūrvabījamātramapi upabhuṅkte tasya savyājavastusaṃgrahasyāpi kṣayatvāt kuto bhāviphalasaṃpadutpādaḥ? tathaiva śīlanivṛtteḥ asthāne sampadupabhogakturapi atimūrkhatayā apūrvākṣeparahitatvāt pūrvākṣepāśeṣopabhogatvācca paścāt sampadbhāvo 'saṃbhavaḥ / śīlapādavihīnasya asya pūrṇasampadbhāvo na kevalaṃ durlabhaḥ, durgatigamanena durgatita utthānam api atidurlabham iti deśanāya-
body.translated_text: One who, having sown a very small seed and obtained abundant fruit, again sows even more seed for the sake of fruit — for that one, the process of gradually increasing the accumulation of great fruit continues uninterruptedly over time, and one can enjoy it for a long time. But one who, through foolishness, consumes even the original seed itself — since even his accumulation of productive goods is exhausted, how can future prosperity arise? Similarly, for one whose moral conduct has lapsed, even though enjoying prosperity in an improper station, through extreme foolishness he lacks the capacity for new meritorious projections, and since the residue of prior projections is consumed — afterward the arising of prosperity is impossible. Not only is full prosperity difficult for one lacking the foundation of moral conduct, but rising out of a bad destiny after falling into it is also extremely difficult — thus, in order to teach this —

children.text: yadā svatantraḥ sthitisāmarūpyam ayaṃ svacintāṃ yadi no karoti /
children.translated_text: When one is autonomous and has the means of maintaining one's position, if this one does not act in his own interest,

children.text: darīprapāte paratantratāptau ka enamuttthāpayitā hi paścāt // Madhy_2.5 //
children.translated_text: who will lift him up afterward, when he has fallen into a precipice and come under another's power? // Madhy 2.5 //

body.text: ityuktama / yadyasau tadā anukūlajanapadasthito bandhamuktaśūravat svacchandaḥ, parādhīnatāmapraviṣṭaḥ san devamanuṣyādilokasthitaḥ svacintāṃ na karoti, sādhiṣṭadarīsamutsṛṣṭabaddhaśūravad durgatiṃgatamenaṃ paścāt ka uttthāpayiṣyati / ata eva pīḍanāya niścitameva durgatirbhaviṣyati / tata eva punarmanuṣyeṣu upapāde 'pi dvividhaḥ paripāko 'bhisiddha ityuktam / yatastādṛśo duḥśīlo 'tyadhikadoṣasambhārādhiṣṭhānam-
body.translated_text: Thus it is stated. If he, while situated in a favorable country like a hero freed from bondage, autonomous, not having entered into dependence on another, situated in the world of gods and men — does not act in his own interest, then like a hero who has been hurled into a deep abyss and bound, who will lift him up afterward when he has gone to a bad destiny? Therefore, a bad destiny will certainly occur, leading to his torment. Even when reborn among humans again, a twofold ripening is established — thus it is said. Since such an immoral person is the ground for the accumulation of extremely great faults —

body.text: tato jino dānakathāmudīrya kathāṃ tu śīlānugatāmuvāca /
body.translated_text: Therefore, the <s>Jina</s> (Conqueror), having first taught the discourse on generosity (<s>dāna</s>), then spoke the discourse following upon moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>).

body.text: tasmādeva parājitasakalapāpadharmo jino dānādiguṇāvipraṇāśāya dānakathāsamayānantaraṃ śīlakathāmeva kṛtavān /
body.translated_text: For that very reason, the <s>Jina</s>, whose <s>dharma</s> has conquered all evil, in order to prevent the destruction of virtues such as generosity, immediately after the occasion of teaching generosity, spoke the discourse on moral conduct itself.

body.text: guṇe vivṛddhe khalu śīlabhūmau phalopabhogastu nirantaraṃ syāt // Madhy_2.6 //
body.translated_text: When virtues increase on the ground of moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>), the enjoyment of fruits will be uninterrupted. // Madhy 2.6 //

body.text: sarvaguṇāśrayabhūtatvāt śīlam eva bhūmiḥ / tatra dānādisarvaguṇavivṛddhiścet hetuphalaparamparā uttarottaraṃ kramaśo 'navacchinnarūpeṇa phalasambhāramupavardhayantī dīrghakālam upabhoktuṃ śakyate, anyathā tu na / ato 'nena prakāreṇa-
body.translated_text: Because moral conduct is the ground of all virtues, the ground itself is <s>śīla</s>. Therein, if there is the increase of all virtues such as generosity — the succession of cause and fruit, progressively increasing the accumulation of fruit in an unbroken manner — it can be enjoyed for a long time; otherwise, it cannot. Therefore, in this manner —

children.text: pṛthagjanaśrāvakanaijabodhisvabhāvaniṣṭhasya jinātmajasya /
children.translated_text: For the ordinary being (<s>pṛthagjana</s>), the <s>śrāvaka</s> (hearer), the one established in innate <s>bodhi</s> (self-arisen awakening), and the child of the <s>Jina</s> (<s>Bodhisattva</s>),

children.text: na heturastyabhyudayāya śīlād ṛte ca niḥśreyasahetave 'nyaḥ // Madhy_2.7 //
children.translated_text: there is no other cause for worldly prosperity (<s>abhyudaya</s>) apart from moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>), nor another cause for the highest good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>). // Madhy 2.7 //

body.text:
yathā- "ime khalu punardaśākuśalāḥ karmapathā adhimātratvādāsevitā [bhāvitā] bahulīkṛtā nirayaheturmadhyatvāt tiryagyoniheturmṛdutvādyamalokahetuḥ / tatra prāṇātipāto nirayamupanayati, tiryagyonimupanayati, yamalokamupanayati / atha cetpunarmanuṣyeṣu upapadyate, dvau vipākāvabhinirvartayati alpāyuṣkatāṃ ca bahuglānyatāṃ ca / adattādānaṃ .........peyālaṃ.........'parīttabhogatāṃ ' ca 'sādhāraṇabhogatāṃ' ca / kāmamithyācāro ... anājāneyaparivāratāṃ ca sasapatnadāratāṃ ca / mṛṣāvādo.......abhyākhyānabahulatāṃ ca parairvisaṃvādanatāṃ ca / paiśunyaṃ......bhinnaparivāratāṃ ca hīnaparivāratāṃ ca / pāruṣyaṃ........amanāpaśravaṇatāṃ ca kalahavacanaṃ ca / tāṃ saṃbhinnapralāpo.......anādeyavacanatāṃ ca aniścitapratibhānatāṃ ca / abhidhyā........asaṃtuṣṭitāṃ ca mahecchatāṃ ca / vyāpādo.......ahitaiṣitāṃ ca parotpīḍanatāṃ ca / mithyādṛṣṭiḥ [nirayamupanayati, tiryagyonimupanayati, yamalokamupanayati / atha cetpunarmanuṣyeṣu upapadyate, dvau vipākāvabhinirvartayati] kudṛṣṭipatitaśca bhavati śaṭhaśca māyāvī / evaṃ khalu mahato 'parimāṇasya duḥkhaskandhasya ime daśākuśalāḥ karmapathāḥ samudāgamāya saṃvartante /" "punaḥ kuśalānāṃ karmapathānāṃ samādānaheto[rdeva] manuṣyādyupapattimādiṃ kṛtvā yāvadbhavāgramityupapattayaḥ prajñāyante / tata uttaraṃ ta eva daśa kuśalāḥ karmapathāḥ prajñākāreṇa paribhāvyamānāḥ prādeśikacittatayā traidhātukottrastamānasatayā mahākaruṇāvikalatayā
parataḥ śravaṇānugamena ghoṣānugamena ca śrāvakayānaṃ saṃvartayanti / tata uttarataraṃ pariśodhitā aparapraṇeyatayā [svayaṃbhūtvānukūlatayā] svayamabhisaṃbodhanatayā [parato 'parimārgaṇatayā] mahākaruṇopāyavikalatayā gambhīredaṃ- pratyayānubodhanena pratyekabuddhayānaṃ saṃvartayati / tata uttarataraṃ pariśodhitā vipulāpramāṇatayā mahākaruṇopetatayā upāyakauśalasaṃgṛhītatayā saṃbaddhamahāpraṇidhānatayā sarvasattvāparityāgatayā buddhajñānavipulādhyālambanatayā bodhisattvabhūmipariśuddhayai pāramitāpariśuddhayai caryāvipulatvāya saṃvartante /" ityādi vistareṇoktavat ato 'nenaprakāreṇa taddaśakuśalamārgātiriktaṃ pṛthagjanaśrāvakapratyekabuddhabodhisattvānāṃ yathāyogam abhyudayasya saṃsārasukhasya, niḥśreyasaḥ sukhaduḥkhābhāvasvabhāvasya muktilakṣaṇasya prāpterupāyo 'nyo nāstīti samupadiṣṭam / yo 'sau dvitīyacittotpādabodhisattvaḥ-
body.translated_text: As follows: 'These ten unwholesome courses of action, when practiced, cultivated, and made abundant to an intense degree, are the cause of hell; to a moderate degree, the cause of the animal realm; to a mild degree, the cause of the world of <s>Yama</s>. Therein, killing leads to hell, leads to the animal realm, leads to the world of <s>Yama</s>. And if one is reborn among humans, it produces two results: short lifespan and much sickness. Stealing... [abbreviated]... leads to meagerness of possessions and sharing of possessions. Sexual misconduct... leads to having a low-born retinue and having a co-wife. False speech... leads to being subject to much false accusation and being deceived by others. Slander... leads to having a divided retinue and an inferior retinue. Harsh speech... leads to hearing unpleasant things and quarrelsome speech. Idle talk... leads to one's words not being heeded and to uncertain eloquence. Covetousness... leads to dissatisfaction and great desire. Ill-will... leads to desiring harm for others and tormenting others. Wrong view [leads to hell, leads to the animal realm, leads to the world of <s>Yama</s>. And if one is reborn among humans, it produces two results:] one falls into wrong views and becomes cunning and deceitful. Thus indeed these ten unwholesome courses of action conduce to the arising of a great, immeasurable mass of suffering.' 'Furthermore, by reason of undertaking the wholesome courses of action, rebirths are understood beginning with rebirth among <s>devas</s> (gods) and humans up to the peak of existence. Beyond that, those same ten wholesome courses of action, when cultivated with the aspect of wisdom, with a limited mind, with a mind terrified of the three realms, lacking great compassion, through following hearing from others and following sounds, conduce to the <s>śrāvaka</s> vehicle. Still beyond that, when further purified, through not being led by others, through being disposed to self-awakening, through awakening by oneself, through not seeking from others, through lacking the means of great compassion, through understanding this profound dependent origination, it conduces to the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle. Still further beyond that, when purified, through vastness and immeasurability, through being endowed with great compassion, through being embraced by skillful means, through being connected with great vows, through not abandoning any sentient being, through having vast reference to <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge, they conduce to the purification of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> stages, the purification of the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), and the vastness of practice.' And so forth as stated in detail. Therefore, in this manner, it has been taught that apart from those ten wholesome paths, there is no other means for the attainment of higher rebirth — the happiness of <s>saṃsāra</s> — and of the highest good — liberation whose nature is the absence of happiness and suffering — for ordinary beings, <s>śrāvakas</s>, <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> respectively. As for that <s>Bodhisattva</s> of the second arising of the mind:

children.text: yathā samudro hi śavena sārdham amaṅgalenāpi ca maṅgalaṃ vā /
children.translated_text: Just as the ocean indeed [will not remain] together with a corpse, [whether] inauspicious or auspicious,

children.text: tathā hi śīlādhikṛto mahātmā samaṃ na tiṣṭhāsati duṣṭaśīlaiḥ // Madhy_2.8 //
children.translated_text: so the great-souled one devoted to <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct) will not remain together with those of corrupt conduct. (Madhyamakāvatāra 2.8)

body.text: amaṃgalamiti akuśalaparyāyaḥ / yathoktaśīlapāramitāvibhedākhyānam-
body.translated_text: 'Inauspicious' is a synonym for unwholesome. The explanation of the divisions of the <s>śīlapāramitā</s> (perfection of moral conduct) as stated:

body.text:
kutaśca kiṃ kutra vivarjitañca trike gṛhīte sati yaddhi śīlam /
vadanti tallaukikapāramīti /
body.translated_text: 'From what source, of what kind, where abandoned, and what is <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct) when grasped with respect to three — that they call the worldly perfection.'

children.text: tacchīlaṃ triṣvavalambitaṃ sat laukikapāramiteti ākhyāyate /
children.translated_text: That <s>śīla</s>, when dependent on the three, is called the worldly perfection.

children.text: alaukikaṃ tat triṣu rāgaśūnyam // Madhy_2.9 //
children.translated_text: The supramundane [perfection] is that which is free from attachment with respect to the three. (Madhyamakāvatāra 2.9)

body.text: tadevaśīlaṃ yathoktālambanatrayarahitaṃ syācced alaukikapāramitetyucyate / yathoktabhūmiguṇānuvādena śīlapāramitāvasthāpariniṣpattimāha-
body.translated_text: That same <s>śīla</s>, if it were devoid of the threefold object as stated, would be called the supramundane perfection. Stating the completion of the <s>śīlapāramitā</s> stage through a description of the qualities of the stage as stated:

children.text: jinātmajendūdgatanirmalāpi bhavābhavaiṣā vimalā bhavaśrīḥ /
children.translated_text: This pure glory of existence, immaculate like the moon risen from the child of the <s>Jina</s> (Victor), free from the stains of existence and non-existence,

children.text: śaradṛtoścāndramasīprabheva jaganmanastāpamapākaroti // Madhy_2.10 //
children.translated_text: like the moonlight of the autumn season, removes the mental anguish of the world. (Madhyamakāvatāra 2.10)

body.text: vimaleti daśakuśalakarmamārgavimalatvād dvitīyabodhisattvabhūmeranvarthaṃ nāma / yathā nirmalā śaraccandraprabhā janasaṃtāpam apākaroti tathā jinaputrendūdgateyaṃ vimalāpi duḥśīlotpannaṃ manaḥsaṃtāpaṃ nivartayati / asyā asaṃsārāntargatatvād na bhavo 'pitu bhavaśrīḥ, sarvaguṇasampadāṃ tadanugatatvāt, caturdvīpaiśvaryasampadhetutvācca /
body.translated_text: '<s>Vimalā</s>' (Stainless) is the fitting name of the second <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage because of the stainlessness of the ten wholesome courses of action. Just as the stainless moonlight of autumn removes the distress of people, so this [stage], risen like a moon from the child of the <s>Jina</s>, though itself stainless, removes the mental anguish arising from corrupt conduct. Because it is not contained within <s>saṃsāra</s>, it is not [mere] existence but rather the glory of existence, since all perfections of qualities follow it, and because it is the cause of the sovereignty of the four continents.

body.text: iti madhyamakāvatārabhāṣye dvitīyaścittotpādaḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Madhyamakāvatārabhāṣya</s>, the second arising of the mind.

body.text: 3. tṛtīyaścittotpādaḥ
body.translated_text: 3. The Third Arising of the Mind

body.text: samprati tṛtīyacittotpādam adhikṛtyottacyate-
body.translated_text: Now, regarding the third arising of the mind, it is stated:

body.text: aśeṣajñeyendhanadāhakāgniprabhodbhavād bhūmiriyaṃ tṛtīyā /
body.translated_text: From the arising of the fire-radiance that burns the fuel of all knowable objects, this third stage

body.text: prabhākarī ................ prabhākarīti tu tṛtīyabodhisattvabhūmināma / punariyaṃ kasmāt prabhākarīti ced anvarthameva / tatsamaye aśeṣajñeyendhanadāhakajñānāgneḥ śāntyātmakaprabhodbhavād bhūmiriyaṃ prabhākarītyucyate / tṛtīyacittotpādasya
body.translated_text: is called <s>Prabhākarī</s> (Luminous)... <s>Prabhākarī</s> is the name of the third <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage. Why is it called <s>Prabhākarī</s>? It is fitting, for at that time, from the arising of the radiance of the pacifying nature of the fire of knowledge that burns the fuel of all knowable objects, this stage is called <s>Prabhākarī</s>. Of the third arising of the mind,

body.text: ............... taṃ sugatasya putraṃ tadā ravistāmra ivāvibhāti // Madhy_3.1 //
body.translated_text: ... then that child of the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One) shines forth like a reddish sun. (Madhyamakāvatāra 3.1)

body.text: yathā sūryaudayāvasthāyāḥ pūrvaṃ tāmra iva avabhāsate tathā bodhisattve 'pi tatra jñānam ābhāsate / tādṛgjñānābhāsaprāptasya tasya bodhisattvasya kṣāntipāramitāviśeṣatādeśanārthamuktam-
body.translated_text: Just as the sun, before the state of its rising, appears reddish, so too knowledge shines forth in the <s>Bodhisattva</s> at that stage. In order to teach the special quality of the <s>kṣāntipāramitā</s> (perfection of patience) for that <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has attained such a radiance of knowledge, it is said:

children.text: akopapātrasya hi tasya kāyāt sahāsthimāṃsaṃ yadi ko 'pi kṛntāt /
children.translated_text: If someone were to cut from the body of this one, who is a vessel of non-anger, together with bones and flesh,

children.text: palaṃ palaṃ dīrghanikṛntane 'pi nikṛntake kṣāntiratīva tasya // Madhy_3.2 //
children.translated_text: limb by limb, even in a prolonged cutting, his patient endurance toward the cutter is indeed supreme. (Madhyamakāvatāra 3.2)

body.text: bodhisattvaḥ paracittānurakṣaṇārthatvāt tādṛgjñānavatvācca yena paradveṣacittādhāratvatrikālanirarthakatvaṃ saṃdehāspadatvañca na syuḥ tādṛksvabhāvakāyavākcittāvatārasākṣī nāsti / akopapātrasya yadi ko 'pi viśeṣaṇam / yadi tādṛkprāṇinā tasya bodhisattvasya kāyato sāsthimāṃsaṃ pratipalaṃ viramya viramya ciraṃ nikṛntite 'pi tādṛkkṛntakāya na kevalaṃ cittavyāroṣo na bhavati apitu, tadakuśalakarmapratyayaṃ narakaduḥkhādiviśeṣam avalambya bodhisattve 'tiviśiṣṭā kṣāntireva jāyate / api ca-
body.translated_text: Because the <s>Bodhisattva</s> acts for the purpose of guarding the minds of others, and because he possesses such knowledge, there is no witness of such entry of body, speech, and mind by nature that [the cutter's] state of being a basis of hostile mind, its purposelessness across the three times, and its being a ground of doubt would not exist. 'Who is a vessel of non-anger' is the qualifying expression. If some such being, from the body of that <s>Bodhisattva</s>, were to cut [his flesh] together with bones and flesh, pausing limb by limb, even when cut for a long time — not only does no mental anger arise, but rather, considering the special suffering of hell and so forth caused by the unwholesome <s>karma</s> [of the cutter], a most distinguished patience indeed arises in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. Moreover:

children.text: yataḥ sa dharmān pratibimbarūpān nirātmadṛk paśyati bodhisattvaḥ /
children.translated_text: Because that <s>Bodhisattva</s>, seeing without self, sees all <s>dharmas</s> as having the form of reflections,

children.text: tataḥ kathaṃ kena kimasti chinnaṃ kadāpi vā kṣāntimupeti cāso // Madhy_3.3 //
children.translated_text: therefore, how, by whom, or what is cut at any time? And [yet] he attains patience. (Madhyamakāvatāra 3.3)

body.text: tadakuśalakarmapratyayaṃ narakādiduḥkhaviśeṣam avalambya na kevalaṃ viśeṣeṇa kṣānto 'pitu yataḥ sa sarvadharmān api pratibimbavat paśyan ātmātmīyasaṃjñānivṛttaḥ tasmād api kṣāntatara eva / api śabdastu kṣāntihetusaṃgrahārtham / kṣāntiriyaṃ na kevalaṃ bodhisattvānurūpo dharmo 'pitu taditarasakalaguṇarakṣāhetubhūtatvād akṣāntavat krodhavyāvṛttirapi yuktā vyākhyātā-
body.translated_text: Considering the special suffering of hell and so forth produced by the unwholesome <s>karma</s> of [the cutter], not only is he especially patient, but because he sees all <s>dharmas</s> like reflections, with the cessation of the notion of self and what belongs to self, he is therefore even more patient. The word 'moreover' is for the purpose of encompassing the causes of patience. This patience is not merely a quality befitting <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, but because it is the cause of protecting all other qualities, the turning away from anger, like impatience, is also rightly explained:

children.text: prakupyate yadyapakāriṇe 'tra kimatra kopo vinivartitaḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: If one becomes angry at a wrongdoer here, would anger have undone the wrong?

children.text: ato 'tra kopo hi nirarthako 'smin paratra loke 'pi viruddha eva // Madhy_3.4 //
children.translated_text: Therefore anger here is indeed purposeless, and in the next world too it is positively harmful. (Madhyamakāvatāra 3.4)

body.text: samprati dattaroṣāvasaro 'yaṃ parasmai apakāriṇe krudhyati cet tadānīntanāpakārāvinivṛtteḥ, tadālambanaḥ pratikopo nirarthaka eva, kṛtakāryatvāt / asmai kopo na kevalaṃ vartamāne niṣprayojanaḥ, apitu paraloko 'pi viruddho bhavati, krodhotpāde sati amanāpaparipākākṣepaḥ / yo duścaritakarmaphalaviśeṣopabhogavān mohāt pareṇāhaṃ prapīḍita iti parikalpayan apakāriṇe krodhamutpādayan pratyapakāreṇa tatpīḍanaṃ parājetukāmaścāsau / tasyāpi vyāvartanārthamāha-
body.translated_text: Now, if having been given occasion for anger, this one becomes angry at a wrongdoer, then since the present wrong has not been undone, retaliation directed at that [wrong] is indeed purposeless, as it is already done. Not only is anger purposeless in the present, but the next world too becomes hostile, since when anger arises, there is the incurring of an unpleasant ripening. He who, experiencing the special results of evil actions due to delusion, conceives 'I have been injured by another' and, generating anger at the wrongdoer, wishes to torment that person through retaliation — for the turning away of such a one too, it is said:

children.text: purākṛtasyākuśalasya karmaphalaṃ tu yo naṣṭatayā vivakṣuḥ /
children.translated_text: He who wishes to explain away the fruit of unwholesome <s>karma</s> previously done as having been destroyed —

children.text: parāhitakrodhata eva duḥkhaṃ kathaṃ hi tadbījatayopanītam // Madhy_3.5 //
children.translated_text: how is suffering brought about precisely as the seed through anger at another's harm? (Madhyamakāvatāra 3.5)

body.text: yat śastradhārapātena tatkāye sādhiṣṭhamapakāraduḥkhaṃ śatruṇopasādhitam, tadantyaphalabhūtaṃ pūrvakṛtaprāṇātipātakarmaṇaḥ prāṇināṃ narakatiryagyoniyamalokādi paripākaphalaṃ ghoram anubhūyamānaṃ niṣyandaphalaṃ yaccāvaśiṣṭakleśāśeṣāpriyaphalanivartanahetuḥ / tatkathaṃ punaḥ rvipariṇāmyaiva, auṣadhasya antimamātrāyā ābhyantare-vyādhipratīkārahetutvād vyāroṣaparāpakārābhyām atītāmanāpaphalādapi ativiśiṣṭāpakāraphalasambhāvanāhetutvena ānīyate? atastad vaidyasya vyādhicikitsāhetubhūtatīkṣṇaśalyakarmakriyāvat phaladuḥkhotpādahetoratikṣāntiryuktā / akṣāntistu na kevalam amanāpaparipākātikṣepaheturapitu dīrghasaṃgṛhītapuṇyasambhārakṣayaheturapyastīti deśanārthamuktam-
body.translated_text: That grievous pain of injury inflicted upon his body by the blow of a weapon-edge by an enemy — the terrible ripening fruit of previously committed acts of killing living beings, experienced as maturation in the hells, animal births, the world of <s>Yama</s>, and so forth, which is the final result — serves as the cause for the cessation of all remaining unpleasant fruits of residual <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). How then is it to be transformed? Since the final measure of medicine serves as the cause of counteracting the internal disease, it is brought about through the hostility of others' harm as the cause for the possibility of an even more distinguished fruit of harm than the past unpleasant fruits. Therefore, just like the sharp surgical operation of a physician that serves as the cause for treating disease, supreme patience toward what produces the fruit of suffering is appropriate. Impatience, however, is not merely the cause for casting one toward unpleasant ripening, but is also the cause for the destruction of the accumulation of merit gathered over a long time — for the purpose of teaching this, it is said:

children.text: dānena śīlena samudgataṃ yat puṇyaṃ citaṃ kalpaśatena naśyet /
children.translated_text: Whatever merit has been accumulated over a hundred <s>kalpas</s> (aeons) through generosity (<s>dāna</s>) and moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>) would be destroyed

children.text: kṣaṇena kopājjinaputrakeṣu tasmān na kopādaparaṃ hi pāpam // Madhy_3.6 //
children.translated_text: in an instant by anger toward the children of the <s>Jina</s> (Victor); therefore, there is no sin greater than anger. // Madhyamakāvatāra 3.6 //

body.text: yadi bodhisattvo mahātmā saḥ pudgale viśiṣṭe 'viśiṣṭe vāpi kleśābhyāsavaśapraveśatvād bodhicittotpānneṣu satyabhūtam asatyabhūtaśca doṣam adhikaṃ prajñāpya kṣaṇamātramapi krodhacittotpāde 'pi tanmātreṇaiva pūrvoktadānaśīlapāramitābhyāsotpannaśatakalpasaṃcitapuṇyasaṃbhāro naśyati, abodhisattvena bodhisattvebhya utpādite tu punaḥ kiṃ vaktavyam? tasmāt mahāsāgarajalapramāṇaṃ karṣagaṇanayā niścetumaśakyaṃ tathā tatra paripākasīmā niścetumaśakyaḥ / ata evaṃ sati amanāpaphalākṣepaṃ puṇyakṣayakarañca pāpam akṣānteḥ param aparaṃ nāsti / "mañjuśrīḥ, krodhaḥ krodha iti śatakalpasaṃbhṛtapuṇyopakṣayakaraḥ, tasmāt krodhaḥ krodha ityākhyātaḥ /" punaśca akṣāntāḥ parāpakārāsamarthāstu ātmānameva nāśayanti, samarthā niṣkaruṇāśca svaparanāśakāḥ / anena tu janmata eva-
body.translated_text: If that great-souled <s>Bodhisattva</s>, toward a person — whether distinguished or undistinguished — who has generated <s>bodhicitta</s>, having imputed either a real or unreal fault excessively, due to the force of entry through habitual affliction, generates even a moment of angry thought, by that alone the accumulation of merit gathered over a hundred <s>kalpas</s>, produced through the practice of the previously mentioned perfections of generosity and moral conduct, is destroyed. What then need be said when a non-<s>Bodhisattva</s> generates [anger] toward <s>Bodhisattvas</s>? Therefore, just as the quantity of water in the great ocean cannot be determined by counting drops, so too the limit of its ripening cannot be determined. This being so, there is no other sin (<s>pāpa</s>) greater than impatience, which both casts toward unpleasant fruits and destroys merit. '<s>Mañjuśrī</s>, anger, anger — it destroys the merit accumulated over a hundred <s>kalpas</s>; therefore, anger is called "anger."' Furthermore, those who are impatient but incapable of harming others destroy only themselves; those who are capable and merciless destroy both themselves and others. By this, from birth itself —

body.text: kudarśano 'sajjananīyamāno nayānayajñānavivekahīnaḥ / parasmin kāle nikāyasabhāgaṃ tyaktvā sakopano durgatimeti śīghram /
body.translated_text: Ugly in appearance, shunned by good people, devoid of the discrimination between right and wrong — in a future life, having abandoned his class of rebirth, the angry one quickly goes to a bad destiny.

body.text: yadyete 'kṣāntidoṣāḥ, tadā ke vai tadviparītakṣāntiguṇā iti-
body.translated_text: If these are the faults of impatience, then what indeed are the virtues of patience, which is its opposite? —

body.text: guṇā viruddhāḥ kathitā hyakopāt // Madhy_3.7 //
body.translated_text: The virtues opposite [to the faults of anger] are declared to arise from non-anger. // Madhyamakāvatāra 3.7 //

children.text: sudarśatā sajjanatāgatiśca nayānayajñānapaṭutvamasti /
children.translated_text: Beauty, acceptance by good people, good rebirth, and skill in the knowledge of right and wrong are present;

children.text: anantaraṃ devamanuṣyajanma kṣayaṃ hyakopādupayāti pāpam // Madhy_3.8 //
children.translated_text: subsequently, birth among gods and humans — through non-anger, sin (<s>pāpa</s>) goes to extinction. // Madhyamakāvatāra 3.8 //

body.text: ye 'kṣāntidoṣā uktāstadviruddhāste guṇāḥ kṣānterjñeyāḥ / tadyathā-
body.translated_text: The faults of impatience that have been stated — the virtues opposite to those should be understood as the virtues of patience. Namely:

children.text: pṛthagjano jinaputraśca doṣān guṇān samālokya ca kopakṣāntyoḥ /
children.translated_text: The ordinary being and the child of the <s>Jina</s> (Bodhisattva), having examined the faults and virtues of anger and patience,

children.text: apāsya kopaṃ tarasaiva kṣāntiṃ sadā śrayeccāryajanapraśastām // Madhy_3.9 //
children.translated_text: should quickly cast aside anger and always resort to patience, which is praised by noble people. // Madhyamakāvatāra 3.9 //

body.text: kopakṣāntī tu kopakṣāntyaiva / doṣaguṇau cāpi doṣaguṇau / krodhakṣāntyordoṣaguṇāviti śabdaviniyogaḥ / krodhadoṣastu yathoktaḥ, viparyayeṇa kṣāntiguṇam avagamya akṣāntiṃ tyaktvā sarvakālaṃ kṣāntireva āśrayaṇīyā / adhunā kṣāntipāramitāprabhedadeśanārtham-
body.translated_text: 'Anger and patience' means 'of anger and patience.' 'Faults and virtues' means 'faults and virtues.' The assignment of words is: 'the faults and virtues of anger and patience.' The fault of anger is as stated; by understanding the virtue of patience in the opposite manner, having abandoned impatience, patience alone should be resorted to at all times. Now, for the purpose of teaching the classification of the perfection of patience —

children.text: sambuddhabaudhyai pariṇāmanāpi triṣvāśritā cet khalu laukikīyam /
children.translated_text: Even dedication to the <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) of the perfectly awakened <s>Buddhas</s>, if relying on the three, is indeed mundane.

children.text: buddhatvāya pariṇāmanāyāmapi kā kṣāntiḥ, kena kṣāntiḥ, keṣu prāṇiṣu kṣāntiretattriṣvāśrayeṣu satsu iyaṃ kṣāntipāramitā laukikīti /
children.translated_text: Even in dedication to Buddhahood — who exercises patience? Toward whom is patience exercised? In what beings is patience exercised? — when these three bases are present, this perfection of patience is mundane.

children.text: anāśritā syāt khalu saiva buddhairalaukikī pāramiteti diṣṭā // Madhy_3.10 //
children.translated_text: Without reliance [on the three], that same [patience] is declared by the <s>Buddhas</s> as the supramundane <s>pāramitā</s> (perfection). // Madhyamakāvatāra 3.10 //

body.text: tasyāṃ bhūmau bodhisattvasya kṣāntipāramitā yathā viśuddhayati tathaiva-
body.translated_text: On that stage, just as the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s perfection of patience is purified, so also —

children.text: abhijñatāṃ dhyānamito 'tra bhūmau jinasya putro hatarāgavairaḥ /
children.translated_text: The child of the <s>Jina</s> attains the supernatural cognitions (<s>abhijñā</s>) through <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) on this stage, having destroyed passion and enmity;

children.text: bhavatyasau laukikakāmarāgau nihantumatyantatayā ca śaktaḥ // Madhy_3.11 //
children.translated_text: he also becomes capable of utterly destroying worldly sensual desire (<s>kāmarāga</s>). // Madhyamakāvatāra 3.11 //

body.text: dhyānamiti dhyānaśabdastu upalakṣaṇārthaḥ, samāpattyapramāṇānāmapi grahaṇaṃ bhavati / yathātṛtīyabodhisattvabhūmāvuktavat- "so 'syāṃ prabhākaryāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthito bodhisattvo dharmānudharmapratipattiheto rviviktaṃ kāmairviviktaṃ pāpakairakuśaladharmaiḥ savitarkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ prītisukhaṃ prathamaṃ dhyānamupasaṃpadya viharati / sa vitarkavicārāṇāṃ vyupaśamādadhyātmasaṃprasādāccetasa ekotībhāvādavitarkamavicāraṃ samādhijaṃ prītisukhaṃ dvitīyadhyānamupasaṃpadya viharati / sa prītervirāgādupekṣako viharati smṛtimān saṃprajānan / sukhaṃ na kāyena pratisaṃvedayati yattadāryā ācakṣante- upekṣakaḥ smṛtimān / sukhavihārī niṣprītikaṃ tṛtīyaṃ dhyānamusaṃpadya viharati / sa sukhasya ca prahāṇādduḥkhasya ca prahāṇātpūrvameva ca saumanasyadaurmanasyayorastaṃgamādaduḥkhāsukhamupekṣāsmṛtipariśuddhaṃ caturthaṃ dhyānamupasaṃpadya viharati /" iti, etāni catvāri dhyānāni / catastra ārūpyasamāpattayastu- tadyathā- "sa sarvaśo rūpasaṃjñānāṃ samatikramāt pratighasaṃjñānāmastaṃgamānnānātvasaṃjñānāmamanasikārādanantakamākāśamityākāśānantyāyatanamupasaṃpadya viharati / sa sarvaśa ākāśānantyāyatanasamatikramādanantaṃ vijñānamiti vijñānānantyāyatanamupasaṃpadya viharati / sa sarvaśo vijñānānantyāyatanasamatikramānnāsti kiṃcidityākiṃcanyāyatanamupasaṃpadya viharati / sa sarvaśa ākiṃcanyāyatanasamatikramānnaiva saṃjñā nāsaṃjñāpi iti saṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanamupasaṃpadya viharati /" imāścatastra ārūpyasamāpattayaḥ / catvāro 'pramāṇāstu evam- "sa maitrīsahagatena cittena vipulena mahadatenādvayenāpramāṇenāvaireṇāsapatnenānāvaraṇenāvyābādhena sarvatrānugatena dharmadhātuparame loke ākāśadhātuparyavasāne sarvāvantaṃ lokaṃ spharitvopasaṃpadya viharati / evaṃ karuṇāsahagatena cittena / muditāsahagatena cittena / upekṣāsahagetana cittena viharati /"
body.translated_text: The word '<s>dhyāna</s>' (meditation) is used as a general designation, [so that] the attainments (<s>samāpatti</s>) and the immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>) are also included. As stated regarding the third <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage: 'That <s>Bodhisattva</s>, established on this <s>Prabhākarī</s> (Luminous) <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage, for the purpose of practice in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s>, secluded from sensual desires, secluded from unwholesome and unskillful <s>dharmas</s>, enters and abides in the first <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), which is accompanied by initial application (<s>vitarka</s>) and sustained application (<s>vicāra</s>), born of seclusion, and endowed with joy (<s>prīti</s>) and happiness (<s>sukha</s>). Through the subsiding of initial and sustained application, through inner tranquility, through one-pointedness of mind, without initial application, without sustained application, he enters and abides in the second <s>dhyāna</s>, which is born of concentration (<s>samādhi</s>) and endowed with joy and happiness. Through detachment from joy, he abides in equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>), mindful and clearly comprehending. He experiences happiness with the body — that which the Noble Ones declare: "He who is equanimous, mindful, and dwells in happiness" — he enters and abides in the third <s>dhyāna</s>, which is without joy. Through the abandonment of happiness and the abandonment of suffering, and through the prior disappearance of mental pleasure and displeasure, he enters and abides in the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>, which is neither painful nor pleasant, purified by equanimity and mindfulness.' These are the four <s>dhyānas</s>. The four formless attainments (<s>ārūpyasamāpatti</s>) are as follows: 'Through the complete transcendence of perceptions of form, through the disappearance of perceptions of resistance, through non-attention to perceptions of diversity, [thinking] "Space is infinite," he enters and abides in the sphere of infinite space (<s>ākāśānantyāyatana</s>). Through the complete transcendence of the sphere of infinite space, [thinking] "Consciousness is infinite," he enters and abides in the sphere of infinite consciousness (<s>vijñānānantyāyatana</s>). Through the complete transcendence of the sphere of infinite consciousness, [thinking] "There is nothing at all," he enters and abides in the sphere of nothingness (<s>ākiṃcanyāyatana</s>). Through the complete transcendence of the sphere of nothingness, [thinking] "Neither perception nor non-perception," he enters and abides in the sphere of neither perception nor non-perception (<s>naiva-saṃjñā-nāsaṃjñāyatana</s>).' These are the four formless attainments. The four immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>) are thus: 'With a mind accompanied by <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), vast, great, non-dual, immeasurable, without enmity, without hostility, without obstruction, without harm, pervading everywhere, reaching to the highest limit of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality), reaching to the boundary of the <s>ākāśadhātu</s> (space-element), having pervaded the entire world, he enters and abides. Likewise with a mind accompanied by <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion). With a mind accompanied by <s>muditā</s> (sympathetic joy). With a mind accompanied by <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity), he abides.'

body.text: pañcābhijñāstu, tadyathā- "so 'nekavidhāṃ ṛddhividhiṃ pratyanubhavati / pṛthivīmapi kampayati / eko 'pi bhūtvā bahudhā bhavati / bahudhāpi bhūtvaiko bhavati / āvirbhāvaṃ tirobhāvamapi pratyanubhavati / tiraḥ kuḍayaṃ tiraḥprākāraṃ parvatamapyasajjan gacchati tadyathāpi nāma ākāśe / ākāśe 'pi paryaṅkena krāmati tadyathāpi nāma pakṣiśakuniḥ / pṛthivyāmapyunmajjananimajjanaṃ karoti tadyathāpi nāma udake / udake 'pyamajjan gacchati tadyathāpi pṛthivyām / dhūmayati prajvalati, tadyathāpi nāma mahānagniskandhaḥ / svakāyādapi mahāvāridhārā utsṛjati tadyathāpi nāma mahāmeghaḥ / yābhirvāridhārābhirayaṃ trisāhastramahāsāhasro lokadhāturādīptaḥ pradīptaḥ saṃprajvalito 'gninā ekajvālībhūto nirvāpyate / imāvapi candrasūryāvevaṃmaharddhiko evaṃmahānubhāvo pāṇinā parāmṛśati parimārṣṭi yāvad brahmalokamapi kāyena vaśaṃ vartayati /" ityete ṛddhayabhijñāḥ /
body.translated_text: The five supernatural cognitions (<s>abhijñā</s>) are as follows: 'He experiences manifold kinds of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhividhi</s>). He causes the earth to tremble. Having been one, he becomes many; having been many, he becomes one. He experiences appearing and disappearing. He passes unobstructed through walls, ramparts, and even mountains, as if through space. He moves cross-legged through space, as if he were a winged bird. He dives in and out of the earth as if it were water. He walks upon water without sinking, as if on earth. He emits smoke and blazes like a great mass of fire. He releases great streams of water from his body, like a great rain cloud. By those streams of water, this trichiliocosm (<s>trisāhasramahāsāhasra-lokadhātu</s>), ablaze, burning, and enveloped in flames as a single conflagration, is extinguished. These very sun and moon, of such great supernatural power and might, he touches and strokes with his hand; he exercises mastery over [everything] up to the <s>Brahmaloka</s> (world of <s>Brahmā</s>) with his body.' These are the supernatural powers of <s>ṛddhi</s> (magical ability).

body.text: "sa divyena śrotradhātunā [viśuddhenā] tikrāntamānuṣyakena ubhayān śabdān śṛṇoti divyān mānuṣyakān, sūkṣmānaudārikāṃśca / ye dūre 'ntike vā antaśo daṃśamaśakakīṭamakṣikāṇāmapi śabdān śṛṇoti / [eṣā divyā śrotrābhijñā] //"
body.translated_text: 'With the divine ear-element (<s>divyaśrotradhātu</s>), purified, surpassing the human, he hears both kinds of sounds — divine and human, subtle and gross — whether far or near, down to the sounds of gadflies, mosquitoes, insects, and flies.' This is the divine ear (<s>divyaśrotra</s>) supernatural cognition.

body.text: "sa parasattvānāṃ parapudgalānāṃ cetasaiva cittaṃ yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / sarāgaṃ cittaṃ sarāgacittamiti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / virāgaṃ cittaṃ virāgacittamiti prajānāti / sadoṣaṃ, vigatadoṣaṃ, samohaṃ, vigatamohaṃ, sakleśaṃ, niḥkleśaṃ, parīttaṃ, vipulaṃ, mahadataṃ, apramāṇaṃ, saṃkṣiptaṃ, [vistīrṇaṃ], samāhitaṃ, asamāhitaṃ, vimuktaṃ, avimuktaṃ, sāṅganam, anaṅganam, audārikaṃ cittamaudārikacittamiti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / anaudārikaṃ cittamanaudārikaṃ cittamiti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / iti parasattvānāṃ parapudgalānāṃ cetasaiva cittaṃ yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / [ityeṣā paracittajñānābhijñā] //"
body.translated_text: "He knows the minds of other beings and other persons accurately by his own mind. He knows a mind with passion as 'a mind with passion'; a mind free from passion as 'a mind free from passion'; a mind with hatred, free from hatred; with delusion, free from delusion; with affliction, free from affliction; narrow, vast, great, immeasurable, concentrated, unconcentrated, collected, uncollected, liberated, unliberated, with stain, without stain; a gross mind as 'a gross mind'; a non-gross mind as 'a non-gross mind' — he knows accurately. Thus he knows the minds of other beings and other persons by his own mind. [This is the <s>abhijñā</s> (supernormal knowledge) of knowing the minds of others.]"

body.text: "so 'nekavidhaṃ pūrvanivāsamanusmarati / ekāmapi jātimanusmarati / dve tistrañcatastraḥ pañca daśa viṃśatiḥ triṃśataṃ catvāriṃśataṃ pañcāśataṃ jātiśata[sahastra]manusmarati / anekānyapi jātiśatāni / [anekānyapi jātisahastrāṇi] anekānyapi jātiśatasahastrāṇi / saṃvartakalpamapi vivartakalpamapi / anekānapi saṃvartavivartakalpānapyanusmarati / kalpaśatamapi kalpasahastramapi kalpaśatasahastramapi kalpakoṭīmapi kalpakoṭīśatamapi kalpakoṭīsahastramapi kalpakoṭīśatasahasramapi yāvadanekānyapi kalpakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇyanusmarati-amunnāhamāsaṃ evaṃnāmā / evaṃgotraḥ evaṃjātiḥ evamāhāra evamāyuḥpramāṇaḥ evaṃcirasthitikaḥ evaṃ sukhaduḥkhapratisaṃvedī / so 'haṃ tataścyuto 'tropapannaḥ / tataścyuta ihopapannaḥ / iti sākāraṃ soddeśaṃ sanimittamanekavidhaṃ pūrvanivāsamanusmarita / [eṣā pūrvanivāsānusmṛtyabhijñā] //"
body.translated_text: "He recalls many kinds of previous abodes. He recalls one birth, two, three, four, five, ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, a hundred, a thousand births; many hundreds of births, many thousands of births, many hundreds of thousands of births; a <s>saṃvartakalpa</s> (dissolution eon), a <s>vivartakalpa</s> (evolution eon); many dissolution and evolution eons; a hundred <s>kalpas</s>, a thousand <s>kalpas</s>, a hundred thousand <s>kalpas</s>, a <s>koṭi</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, a hundred <s>koṭis</s>, a thousand <s>koṭis</s>, a hundred thousand <s>koṭis</s>, up to many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭi-niyutas</s> of <s>kalpas</s> — [remembering:] 'There I was, of such a name, such a clan, such a birth, such food, such a lifespan, of such long duration, experiencing such happiness and suffering. Having passed away from there, I was reborn here. Having passed away from there, I was reborn here.' Thus with form, with detail, with characteristics, he recalls many kinds of previous abodes. [This is the <s>abhijñā</s> of recollecting previous abodes.]"

body.text: "sa divyena cakṣuṣā viśuddhenātikrāntamānuṣyakeṇa sattvān paśyati cyavamānānupapadyamānān suvarṇān durvarṇān sugatān durgatān praṇītān hīnān / yathākarmopagān sattvān yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti- ime bhavantaḥ sattvāḥ kāyaduścaritena samanvāgatā vāgduścaritena samanvāgatā manoduścaritena samanvāgatāḥ āryāṇāmapavādakā mithyādṛṣṭayaḥ mithyādṛṣṭikarmasamādānahetostaddhetuṃ tatpratyayaṃ kāyasya bhedātparaṃ maraṇādapāyadurgativinipātanirayeṣūpapadyante / ime punarbhavantaḥ sattvāḥ kāyasucaritena samanvāgatā vāksucaritena samanvāgatā manaḥsucaritena samanvāgatā āryāṇāmanapavādakāḥ / samyagdṛṣṭikarmasamādānahetostaddhetuṃ tatpratyayaṃ kāyasya bhedāt paraṃ maraṇātsugatau svarge devalokeṣūpapadyanta iti [prajānāti / evaṃ] divyena cakṣuṣā viśuddhenātikrāntamanuṣyeṇa (cyavamānānupapadyamānān) sākāraṃ soddeśaṃ sanimittaṃ sattvān paśyati / yathākarmopagatān sattvān yathābhūtān prajānāti / sa imāni dhyānāni vimokṣān samādhīn samāpattīśca samāpadyate, vyuttiṣṭhate / na ca teṣāṃ vaśenopapadyate 'nyatra yatra bodhyaṅgaparipūriṃ paśyati tatra saṃcintya praṇidhānavaśenopapadyate / tatkasya heto? tathā hi tasya bodhisattvasyopāyakauśalyābhinirhatā cittasaṃtatiḥ //"
body.translated_text: "With the divine eye, purified and surpassing the human, he sees beings dying and being reborn — beautiful and ugly, in good destinies and bad destinies, noble and low. He knows beings accurately as they go according to their <s>karma</s>: 'These beings, endowed with bodily misconduct, verbal misconduct, and mental misconduct, who revile the noble ones, who hold wrong views, who undertake actions based on wrong views — by that cause and that condition, after the dissolution of the body, after death, they are reborn in the lower realms, bad destinies, perdition, and hells. But these beings, endowed with good bodily conduct, good verbal conduct, and good mental conduct, who do not revile the noble ones, who hold right views, who undertake actions based on right views — by that cause and that condition, after the dissolution of the body, after death, they are reborn in good destinies, in heaven, in the divine realms.' Thus with the divine eye, purified and surpassing the human, he sees beings with form, with detail, with characteristics, and knows beings accurately as they go according to their <s>karma</s>. He attains and emerges from these <s>dhyānas</s> (meditative absorptions), <s>vimokṣas</s> (liberations), <s>samādhis</s> (concentrations), and <s>samāpattis</s> (attainments). Yet he is not reborn by their power; rather, wherever he sees the fulfillment of the factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>), there he is deliberately reborn by the power of his aspiration (<s>praṇidhāna</s>). Why is that? Because the mental continuum of that <s>Bodhisattva</s> is produced by skillful means (<s>upāyakauśalya</s>)."

body.text: ata eva asyāṃ bhūmau bodhisattve dhyānam abhijñāśca sambhavanti kathaṃ sadā laukikarāgadveṣaparikṣayaḥ? capadaṃ tu anuktasaṅgrahārtham, iti tasya mohasyāpi parikṣayo bhavati- katham iti, idamapi yathā sūtre- "sa sarvadharmāṇāmasaṃkrāntitāṃ ca avināśitāṃ ca pratītya pratyayatayā vyavalokayati // tasya bhūyasyā mātrayā sarvāṇi kāmabandhanāni tanūni bhavanti / sarvāṇi rūpabandhanāni sarvāṇi bhavabandhanāni sarvāṇyavidyābandhanāni tanūni bhavanti / dṛṣṭikṛtabandhanāni ca pūrvameva prahīṇāni bhavanti / tasya asya prabhākaryāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthitasya bodhisattvasya anekān kalpān yāvadanekāni kalpakoṭiniyutaśatasahastrāṇi ....peyālaṃ.....anupacayaṃ mithyārāgaḥ prahāṇaṃ gacchati, anupacayaṃ mithyādoṣaḥ prahāṇaṃ gacchati, anupacayaṃ mithyāmohaḥ prahāṇaṃ gacchati /" ityuktam / atastasya rāgo dveṣo mohaśca parikṣīṇo bhavati / kathaṃ hi te sadā laukikakāmarāgāt upahantuṃ samarthā bhaviṣyantīti yathā- "iyaṃ bhavanto jinaputrā bodhisattvasya prabhākarī nāma tṛtīyā bodhisattvabhūmiḥ samāsanirdeśataḥ, yasyāṃ pratiṣṭhito bodhisattvo bhūyastvena indro bhavati devarājastridaśādhipatiḥ kṛtī prabhuḥ sattvānāṃ kāmarāgavinivartanopāyopasaṃhārāya kuśalaḥ sattvān kāmapaṅkādabhyuddhartum", ityuktam / ataḥ sa jinaputro laukikakāmarāgān upahantuṃ samartho bhaviṣyati / evam asya bodhisattvasya tṛtīyabodhisattvabhūmau viśuddhakṣāntipāramitādhyānāparimāṇasamāpatyabhijñā rāgādiparikṣayasya ca niścitaprāptirbhaviṣyatītyuktvā adhunā tu kṣāntipāramitāparyantaṃ pāramitātrayāśrayaviśeṣaṃ sambhārasvabhāvaṃ phalaparisiddhivyavasthāṃ ca prakāśayitum ākhyāyate-

children.text: ime hi dānādimayāḥ tridharmā gṛhibhya uktāḥ sugataistu bhūyaḥ /
children.translated_text: These three <s>dharmas</s> (virtues) beginning with <s>dāna</s> (generosity) are taught by the <s>Sugatas</s> (Well-Gone Ones) especially for householders;

children.text: ta eva puṇyetyapi saṃbhṛtā hi sambuddharūpātmakakāyahetuḥ // Madhy_3.12 //
children.translated_text: and those very same, collected as 'merit' (<s>puṇya</s>), are the cause of the form-body (<s>rūpakāya</s>) of the fully awakened one. // Madhy 3.12 //

body.translated_text: For this very reason, since <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) and the <s>abhijñās</s> (supernormal knowledges) arise in the <s>Bodhisattva</s> on this <s>bhūmi</s> (stage), how is there always the destruction of worldly passion and hatred? The word 'ca' ('and') is for the purpose of including what is unstated — thus his delusion is also destroyed. How? This too, as in the <s>sūtra</s>: "He sees all <s>dharmas</s> as non-transferred and non-destroyed, through dependent origination and conditionality. For him, to a great extent all the bonds of desire (<s>kāma</s>) become thin, all the bonds of form (<s>rūpa</s>), all the bonds of existence (<s>bhava</s>), and all the bonds of ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) become thin. The bonds created by wrong views have been abandoned previously. For this <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on the <s>Prabhākarī</s> (Luminous) <s>bodhisattva-bhūmi</s>, for many <s>kalpas</s> and up to many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭi-niyutas</s> of <s>kalpas</s> ...abbreviation... wrong passion decreases and goes to abandonment, wrong hatred decreases and goes to abandonment, wrong delusion decreases and goes to abandonment." Thus it is stated. Therefore his passion, hatred, and delusion are destroyed. How could they always be capable of being afflicted by worldly desire? As stated: "This, O sons of the Conqueror, is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s third <s>bodhisattva-bhūmi</s> called <s>Prabhākarī</s> (Luminous), in summary. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> established therein is mostly born as <s>Indra</s>, king of the gods, lord of the thirty, accomplished, powerful, skillful in the means of turning beings away from sensual desire, able to rescue beings from the mire of sensuality." Thus it is stated. Therefore that son of the Conqueror will be capable of destroying worldly sensual desires. Thus, having stated that for this <s>Bodhisattva</s> on the third <s>bodhisattva-bhūmi</s> there will be the certain attainment of the purified <s>kṣānti-pāramitā</s> (perfection of patience), <s>dhyāna</s>, the immeasurables, the <s>samāpattis</s>, the <s>abhijñās</s>, and the destruction of passion and the rest — now, to illuminate the special ground of the threefold <s>pāramitā</s> up to <s>kṣānti-pāramitā</s>, the nature of the accumulations, and the establishment of the attainment of fruit, it is said:

body.text: bodhisattvā eva yathoktadānādyāśrayāḥ santi, tathāpi gṛhasthapravrajitabhedena tatra dvayoḥ saṃbhavaṃ vicintya tathoktam / tatra gṛhastheṣu prāyeṇa dānādayastrayo dharmāḥ susādhyāḥ, parivrājakeṣu ca vīryaṃ, dhyānaṃ tathā prajñā / na cetaretarāsaṃbhāvanā / buddhatvahetusambhārau tu dvau staḥ, sa cāsau puṇyasaṃbhāro jñānasaṃbhāraśca / tatra puṇyasambhārastu tāstistraḥ pāramitāḥ santi, jñānasambhāraśca dhyānaṃ prajñā ca / vīryaṃ tūbhayaheturiti vyavasthā / tatra yaḥ puṇyasambhāraḥ sa saṃbuddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ śatapuṇyalakṣaṇasya adabhutasya acintyasya viśvarūpamayasya rūpakāyasya hetuḥ / dharmasvabhāvakāyasya anutpādalakṣaṇasya hetustu jñānasambhāraḥ / samprati āśrayādimāhātmyena svamahatvam uktvā tṛtīyabodhisattvabhūmyavasthā samākhyāyate-
body.translated_text: <s>Bodhisattvas</s> alone are the basis for the aforesaid <s>dāna</s> and the rest; nevertheless, considering the possibility of both in the division of householders and renunciants, it is thus stated. Among householders, the three <s>dharmas</s> beginning with <s>dāna</s> are generally easy to accomplish; and among renunciants, <s>vīrya</s> (effort), <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), and <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom). Nor is the impossibility of the other [in each] implied. The two accumulations that are the causes of Buddhahood are the accumulation of merit (<s>puṇyasambhāra</s>) and the accumulation of knowledge (<s>jñānasambhāra</s>). The accumulation of merit consists of those three <s>pāramitās</s>; the accumulation of knowledge consists of <s>dhyāna</s> and <s>prajñā</s>. <s>Vīrya</s> is established as the cause of both. The accumulation of merit is the cause of the <s>rūpakāya</s> (form body) of the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> — that wondrous, inconceivable, manifold form-body marked by the hundred marks of merit. The accumulation of knowledge is the cause of the <s>Dharmakāya</s> (truth body) whose characteristic is the unborn (<s>anutpāda</s>). Now, having proclaimed its own greatness through the excellence of its ground and so forth, the state of the third <s>bodhisattva-bhūmi</s> is described —

body.text:
prabhākarīyaṃ jinaputrasūrye tamaḥ svakaṃ pūrvataraṃ vināśya /
samīhate lokatamo vihantuṃ /
body.translated_text: On this <s>Prabhākarī</s> (Luminous) stage, the sun-like son of the Conqueror, having first destroyed his own darkness, strives to destroy the darkness of the world.

body.text: sugataputrasūryasthiteyaṃ prabhākarībhūmiḥ svāśritām avidyāṃ ātmodbhavavighnabhūtāṃ jāyamānāvasthāyāmeva vināśya tatprakāropadeśena tadbhinnānāṃ tṛtīyabhūmyudbhavavighnāndhakāraṃ vihantuṃ samīhate / sa bodhisattvaḥ-
body.translated_text: This <s>Prabhākarī-bhūmi</s>, the abode of the sun-like son of the <s>Sugata</s>, having at the very moment of its arising destroyed the ignorance that resides in oneself — the obscuring darkness — strives to destroy through instruction in its methods the darkness of the third-bhūmi obstructions that affect others.

body.text: na cātra kopo bhuvi tīkṣṇabhūte // Madhy_3.13 //
body.translated_text: And there, even though the stage is intensely sharp, there is no anger. // Madhy 3.13 //

body.text: sa tu doṣāndhakārāṇāṃ pratibandhakānāṃ nāśanena sūryavad atitīkṣṇatāvatāre 'pi doṣayuktajanebhyo na krudhyati / kṣānterativiśiṣṭābhyāsāt karuṇayā santateḥ snigdhatvācca /
body.translated_text: Though he, like the sun, is extremely sharp in his approach to destroying the darkness of faults, he does not become angry at those endowed with faults — because of the supremely special practice of <s>kṣānti</s> (patience) and the tenderness of his mental continuum through <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion).

body.text: madhyamakāvatārabhāṣye tṛtīyaścittotpādaḥ /
body.translated_text: In the <s>Madhyamakāvatāra-bhāṣya</s>: the third arising of the mind.

body.text: 4. caturthaścittotpādaḥ
body.translated_text: 4. The Fourth Arising of the Mind

body.text: samprati dānaśīlakṣāntipāramitābhyo vīryapāramitāyā atirekadeśanādvāreṇa caturthacittotpādamadhikṛtya ākhyāyate-
body.translated_text: Now, regarding the fourth arising of the mind, through the door of teaching the surpassing excellence of the <s>vīrya-pāramitā</s> (perfection of effort) over the <s>pāramitās</s> of <s>dāna</s>, <s>śīla</s>, and <s>kṣānti</s>, it is said —

children.text: guṇā aśeṣā anugamya vīryaṃ dvayostu heturmatipuṇyarāśyoḥ /
children.translated_text: All virtues without exception follow upon <s>vīrya</s> (effort), and it is the cause of both accumulations of wisdom and merit;

children.text: yato bhavet projjvalameva vīryam arciṣmatī bhūḥ khalu sā caturthī // Madhy_4.1 //
children.translated_text: wherever there is blazing <s>vīrya</s> indeed, that fourth stage is called <s>Arciṣmatī</s> (Blazing). // Madhy 4.1 //

body.text: kuśalakarmānutsāhamaye tu sarvathā dānādāpravṛtteḥ sarvaguṇotpādo 'saṃbhavaḥ / pūrvoktaguṇasañcayasamutsuke tu prāptāprāptayorvṛddhiprāptisaṃbhavād yasya kasyacid guṇasya hetustu vīryameva asti / sambhāradvayahetustu pūrvata ākhyātaḥ / tad vīryaṃ svaguṇapariśuddhidvārā yasyāṃ bhūmāvadhijvalati sā tu caturthī bodhisatvabhūmiḥ arciṣmatīti syāt / api ca, kasya hetorarciṣmatīti ākhyāyate-nāmāvatārahetudeśanārtham-
body.translated_text: However, in a state of non-enthusiasm for wholesome <s>karma</s>, since there is no engagement in giving and so forth at all, the arising of all qualities is impossible. But for one who is eager for the accumulation of the aforementioned qualities, since growth and attainment are possible for both what has been attained and what has not, the cause of each and every quality is <s>vīrya</s> (effort) alone. The cause of the two accumulations has been explained previously. That <s>vīrya</s>, through the door of the purification of its own qualities, blazes forth on whichever <s>bhūmi</s> (stage) — that is the fourth <s>bodhisattva-bhūmi</s> called <s>Arciṣmatī</s> (Radiant). Moreover, for what reason is it called <s>Arciṣmatī</s>? For the purpose of teaching the reason for the name —

body.text:
sambodhipakṣasya vibhāvanāto jāto 'vabhāsaḥ sugatasya putre /
tāmraprabhāyā adhikaṃ vibhāti
body.translated_text: "From the cultivation of the constituents of perfect awakening, a radiance has arisen in the son of the <s>Sugata</s>;

body.text: ityuktam / evam asyāṃ bhūmau bodhisattve saptatriṃśad bodhipākṣikadharmabhāvanena pūrvākhyātatāmraprabhāyā viśiṣṭo 'vabhāsa upapadyate / tasmāt samyagjñānāgniprabhopapādena sā bodhisattvabhūmirarciṣmatītyākhyāyate / saptatriṃśad bodhipākṣikā dharmastu evam- catvāri smṛtyupasthānāni, catvāri samyakprahāṇāni, catvāra ṛddhipādāḥ, pañcendriyāṇi, pañca balāni, sapta bodhyaṅgāni āryāṣṭāṅgamārgaścetyuktāḥ / tatra catvāri smṛtyupasthānāni- "jinaputrā, bodhisattvo 'syāmarciṣmatyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau pratiṣṭhito 'dhyātmaṃ kāye kāyānudarśī viharati, ātāpī saṃprajānan smṛtimān vinīya loko 'bhidhyādaurmanasye / bahirdhā kāye (kāyānudarśī viharati, ātāpī saṃprajānan smṛtimān vinīya loke 'bhidhyādaurmanasye) adhyātmaṃ bahirdhā kāye / evamevādhyātmaṃ vedanāsu bahirdhā vedanāsu adhyātmaṃ bahirdhā vedanāsu / evamadhyātmaṃ citte bahirdhā citte 'dhyātmaṃ bahirdhā citte / adhyātmaṃ dharmeṣu dharmānudarśī (viharati ātāpī saṃprajānan smṛtimān) bahirdhā dharmeṣu dharmānudarśī ... evamadhyātmaṃ bahirdhā dharmeṣu... /" iti vistṛtanirdeśavat /
body.translated_text: it shines forth more brilliantly than the copper-colored light." Thus it is said. In this way, on this <s>bhūmi</s>, through the cultivation of the thirty-seven <s>bodhipākṣika dharmas</s> (factors of awakening) by the <s>bodhisattva</s>, a radiance superior to the previously mentioned copper-colored light arises. Therefore, through the arising of the light of the fire of perfect knowledge, that <s>bodhisattva-bhūmi</s> is called <s>Arciṣmatī</s> (Radiant). The thirty-seven <s>bodhipākṣika dharmas</s> are as follows: four <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> (foundations of mindfulness), four <s>samyakprahāṇas</s> (right exertions), four <s>ṛddhipādas</s> (bases of supernatural power), five <s>indriyas</s> (faculties), five <s>balas</s> (powers), seven <s>bodhyaṅgas</s> (factors of awakening), and the <s>āryāṣṭāṅgamārga</s> (noble eightfold path). Among these, the four foundations of mindfulness: "Sons of the <s>Jina</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> established on this <s>Arciṣmatī bodhisattva-bhūmi</s> dwells contemplating the body in the body internally, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and grief regarding the world. He dwells contemplating the body in the body externally, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and grief regarding the world; internally and externally in the body. Likewise, internally in feelings, externally in feelings, internally and externally in feelings. Likewise, internally in the mind, externally in the mind, internally and externally in the mind. He dwells contemplating <s>dharmas</s> in <s>dharmas</s> internally, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful; externally in <s>dharmas</s>... likewise internally and externally in <s>dharmas</s>..." as stated in the detailed exposition.

body.text: catvāri samyakprahāṇāni yathā- "so 'nutpannānāṃ pāpakānāmakuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāmanutpādāya cchandaṃ janayati vyāyacchate vīryamārabhate cittaṃ pragṛhṇāti samyakpraṇidadhāti / utpannānāṃ pāpakānāmakuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ
body.translated_text: The four right exertions are as follows: "He generates desire for the non-arising of unarisen evil, unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>; he strives, applies effort, exerts his mind, and rightly resolves. For the abandonment of arisen evil, unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>,

body.text: prahāṇāya[itipūrvavat] / anutpannānāṃ kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāmutpādāya [itipūrvavat] / utpannānāṃ kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ sthitaye 'saṃpramoṣāya vaipulyāya bhūyobhāvāya (bhāvanāya) paripūraye [cchandaṃ janayati, vyāyacchate- tu pūrvavat] /"
body.translated_text: [he does likewise]. For the arising of unarisen wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, [likewise]. For the maintenance of arisen wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, for their non-confusion, for their abundance, for their increase, for their cultivation, and for their fulfillment, [he generates desire, strives — as before]."

body.text: catvāro ṛddhipādāḥ "chandasamādhiprahāṇasaṃskārasamanvāgataṃ ṛddhipādaṃ bhāvayati vivekaniścitaṃ virāganiścitaṃ nirodhaniścitaṃ vyavasargapariṇataṃ [tadvat] vīrya [samādhiprahāṇasaṃskārasamanvāgataṃ ṛddhipādaṃ] bhāvayati citta [samādhiprahāṇasaṃskārasamanvāgataṃ ṛddhipādaṃ] bhāvayati mīmāṃsā [samādhiprahāṇasaṃskārasamanvāgataṃ ṛddhipādaṃ] bhāvayatītyādi pūrvavat /"
body.translated_text: The four bases of supernatural power: "He cultivates the basis of supernatural power endowed with the formations of exertion and <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) born of desire, determined by seclusion, determined by dispassion, determined by cessation, maturing in relinquishment. Likewise, he cultivates the basis of supernatural power [endowed with the formations of exertion and <s>samādhi</s>] born of effort; he cultivates that born of mind; he cultivates that born of investigation — and so forth as before."

body.text:
pañcendriyāṇi tadyathā- "sa śraddhendriyaṃ bhāvayati [iti tadvat] vivekaniścitaṃ...vīryendriyaṃ....smṛtīndriyaṃ....samādhīndriyaṃ...prajñendriyaṃ...sa / "bhāvayati virāganiścitaṃ ityādi / pañcabalāni tu tānyevāsapakṣaparājitāni pūrvavat /
sapta bodhyaṅgāni- tadyathā- "(sa) smṛti-saṃbodhyaṅgaṃ bhāvayati, [ityādi] dharmapravicaya [bodhyaṅgaṃ] vīrya [saṃbodhyaṅgaṃ] prīti [saṃbodhyaṅgaṃ] prastrabdhi-[saṃbodhyaṅgaṃ] samādhi [saṃbodhyaṅgaṃ] upekṣā [saṃbodhyaṅgaṃ bhāvayati ityādi pūrvavat] /"
body.translated_text: The five faculties, namely: "He cultivates the faculty of <s>śraddhā</s> (faith), likewise determined by seclusion... the faculty of <s>vīrya</s> (effort)... the faculty of <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness)... the faculty of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration)... the faculty of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom)... he cultivates, determined by dispassion, and so forth." The five powers are those very same, undefeated by opponents, as before. The seven factors of awakening, namely: "He cultivates the <s>smṛti-saṃbodhyaṅga</s> (awakening factor of mindfulness), [and so forth] <s>dharmapravicaya</s> (investigation of dharmas), <s>vīrya</s> (effort), <s>prīti</s> (joy), <s>praśrabdhi</s> (tranquility), <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity) [awakening factors — he cultivates, and so forth as before]."

body.text: āryāṣṭāṅgamārgastu yathā- "samyakdṛṣṭiṃ bhāvayati [virāganiścitaṃ nirodha- niścitaṃ vyavasargapariṇataṃ] samyaksaṅkalpaṃ [api pūrvavat] samyagvācaṃ........ samyakkarmāntaṃ......samyagājīvaṃ......samyagvyāyāmaṃ.....samyaksmṛtiṃ...samyaksamādhiṃ /" [bhāvayati ityādi pūrvavat /] asyāṃ bhūmau na kevalaṃ bodhipākṣikabhāvanotpādo 'pitu-
body.translated_text: The noble eightfold path, as follows: "He cultivates <s>samyagdṛṣṭi</s> (right view) [determined by dispassion, determined by cessation, maturing in relinquishment]; <s>samyaksaṅkalpa</s> (right intention) [likewise as before]; <s>samyagvāc</s> (right speech)... <s>samyakkarmānta</s> (right action)... <s>samyagājīva</s> (right livelihood)... <s>samyagvyāyāma</s> (right effort)... <s>samyaksmṛti</s> (right mindfulness)... <s>samyaksamādhi</s> (right concentration)." [He cultivates, and so forth as before.] On this <s>bhūmi</s>, not only does the cultivation of the factors of awakening arise, but also —

body.text: saṃkṣīyate cātmadṛśo 'nuṣaṅgaḥ // Madhy_4.2 //
body.translated_text: the attachment to the view of self is extinguished. || Madhy_4.2 ||

body.text: asyāṃ bhūmau tasya ātmadṛṣṭikṣayo 'pi bhavati- tathā- "jinaputrā, bodhisattvasya asyāmarciṣmatyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sthitasya yānīmāni satkāyadṛṣṭipūrvaṅgamāni ātmasattvajīvapoṣa (puruṣa) pudalaskandhadhātvāyatanābhiniveśasamucchritāni unmarjjitāni nimajjitāni vicintitāni vitarkitāni kelāyitāni mamāyitāni dhanāyitāni niketasthānāni, tāni sarvāṇi vigatāni bhavanti sma /" ityuktam /
body.translated_text: On this <s>bhūmi</s>, the destruction of his <s>ātmadṛṣṭi</s> (self-view) also occurs — thus: "Sons of the <s>Jina</s>, for a <s>bodhisattva</s> established on this <s>Arciṣmatī bodhisattva-bhūmi</s>, all those habitual abodes that are preceded by <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> (view of the personal aggregate), that are elevated through clinging to self, being, life, nourisher, person, <s>pudgala</s>, <s>skandhas</s>, <s>dhātus</s>, and <s>āyatanas</s>, that are rubbed smooth, smoothed down, considered, reflected upon, played with, appropriated as 'mine,' treasured, and made into a dwelling — all those are gone." Thus it is said.

body.text: iti madhyamakāvatārabhāṣye 'rciṣmatī nāma caturthaścittotpādaḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Madhyamakāvatāra-bhāṣya</s>, <s>Arciṣmatī</s> is the name of the fourth generation of mind.

body.text: 5. pañcamaścittotpādaḥ
body.translated_text: 5. The Fifth Generation of Mind

body.text: samprati pañcamacittotpādādhikāraḥ-
body.translated_text: Now the section on the fifth generation of mind —

body.text: sa durjayābhūmigato mahātmā kṣamo na jetuṃ hyapi sarvamāraiḥ /
body.translated_text: That great-souled one, situated on the <s>Durjayā bhūmi</s> (Difficult to Conquer stage), indeed cannot be conquered even by all <s>Māras</s>;

body.text: pañcamabodhisattvabhūmau sthito bodhisattvastu sarvalokadhātusthitairdevaputramārairapi jetuṃ na kṣamaḥ tatpareṣāṃ mārakiṅkarādīnāṃ kaḥ punarvādaḥ? ata eva asyā bhūmernāma sudurjayeti / bodhisattvastu-
body.translated_text: A <s>bodhisattva</s> established on the fifth <s>bodhisattva-bhūmi</s> cannot be conquered even by the <s>devaputra-māras</s> (demon-gods) dwelling in all world-realms — what need to mention <s>Māra</s>'s servants and others? Therefore the name of this <s>bhūmi</s> is <s>Sudurjayā</s> (Very Difficult to Conquer). The <s>bodhisattva</s>, however —

body.text: dhyāne viśiṣṭe sumateśca satyasūkṣmasvabhāvādhigame 'tidakṣaḥ // Madhy_5.1 //
body.translated_text: is supremely skilled in attaining the subtle nature of the truths of the noble ones, and in the excellence of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation). || Madhy_5.1 ||

body.text: jñātavyaḥ / tatra daśapāramitāsu dhyānapāramitaiva ativiśiṣṭā bhavati / sumatīti āryāḥ / teṣāṃ satyāni sumatisatyāni āryasatyānītyarthaḥ / svabhāvastu svarūpam / sūkṣmajñānādhigatasvabhāvastu sūkṣmasvabhāvaḥ, bhadramatisatyānāṃ sūkṣmasvarūpasya jñāne 'tidakṣo bhavati / caturāryasatyāni tu duḥkhasamudayanirodhamārgāḥ / bhagavatā satyaṃ tu dvayameva diṣṭamiti tadyathā- saṃvṛtisatyaṃ paramārthasatyañca / yathā-pitāputrasamāgamasūtre-
body.translated_text: This should be known. Among the ten <s>pāramitās</s>, <s>dhyāna-pāramitā</s> (perfection of meditation) is the most distinguished. <s>Sumati</s> means the noble ones. Their truths are the truths of the noble ones, meaning the <s>āryasatyas</s> (noble truths). <s>Svabhāva</s> means own-nature. The nature attained by subtle knowledge is the subtle nature; he becomes supremely skilled in the knowledge of the subtle own-nature of the truths of the noble ones. The four <s>āryasatyas</s> (noble truths) are: <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering), <s>samudaya</s> (origin), <s>nirodha</s> (cessation), and <s>mārga</s> (path). The <s>Bhagavān</s> declared that truth is precisely twofold, namely: <s>saṃvṛtisatya</s> (conventional truth) and <s>paramārthasatya</s> (ultimate truth). As in the <s>Pitāputrasamāgama-sūtra</s> —

body.text: satya ime duvi lokavidūnāṃ diṣṭa svayaṃ aśruṇitva pareṣām / saṃvṛti yā ca tathā paramārtho satyu na sidhyati kiṃ ca tṛtīyu // ityuktam / madhyamakaśāstre 'pi-
body.translated_text: "Two truths have been taught by the knowers of the world, heard by themselves and not from others: the conventional and likewise the ultimate — a third truth is not found." Thus it is said. In the <s>Madhyamakaśāstra</s> also —

body.text: dve satye samupāśritya buddhānāṃ dharmadeśanā / lokasaṃvṛtisatyaṃ ca satyaṃ ca paramārthataḥ // ityuktam / ataḥ kvasatyadvayātiriktāni anyāni caturāryasatyāni santīti cet- āravyāyate- yadyapi evam, tathāpi heyopādeyayoḥ pṛthak pṛthak hetuphalabhāvadeśanārthaṃm atra caturāryasatyāni uktāni / tatra heyapakṣastu saṃkleśaḥ / tatphalaṃ ca duḥkhasatyam / hetuśca samudayasatyam / upādeyapakṣastu vyavadānam, tasya phalaṃ nirodhasatyam / tatprāptiheturmārgasatyam / tatra duḥkhasamudayamārgasatyānāṃ saṃvṛtisatye 'ntarbhāvaḥ / nirodhasatyaṃ paramārthasatyasvarūpam / tathāparaṃ satyaṃ yat kiṃcit syāt tasyāpi yathāyogaṃ satyadvaye 'ntarbhāva eva niśceyaḥ / kiṃ catuḥsatyātiriktamaparamapi satyamastīti cet? ākhyātam / yathā-bodhisattvapañcamabhūmau - "idaṃ duḥkhamāryasatyamiti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / ayaṃ duḥkhasamudaya āryasatyamiti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / ayaṃ duḥkhanirodha āryasatyamiti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / iyaṃ duḥkhanirodhagāminī pratipadāryasatyamiti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / sa saṃvṛtisatyakuśalaśca bhavati / paramārthasatyakuśalaśca bhavati / lakṣaṇasatyakuśalaśca bhavati / vibhāgasatyakuśalaśca bhavati / nistīraṇasatyakuśalaśca bhavati / vastusatyakuśalaśca bhavati / prabhavasatyakuśalaśca bhavati / kṣayānutpādasatyakuśalaśca bhavati / mārgajñānāvatārasatyakuśalaśca bhavati / sarvabodhisattvabhūmikramānusaṃdhiniṣpādanatayā yāvattathāgatajñānasamudayasatyakuśalaśca bhavati / sa parasattvānāṃ yathāśayasaṃtoṣaṇātsaṃvṛtisatyaṃ prajānāti / ekanayasamavasaraṇātparamārthasatyaṃ prajānāti / svasāmānyalakṣaṇānubodhāllakṣaṇasatyaṃ prajānāti / dharmavibhāgavyavasthānānubodhādvibhāgasatyaṃ prajānāti / skandhadhātvāyatanavyavasthānānubodhānnistīraṇasatyaṃ prajānāti / cittaśarīraprapīḍanopanipātitatvādvastusatyam, gatisaṃdhisaṃbandhanatvātprabhavasatyam, sarvajvaraparidāhātyantopaśamātkṣayānutpādasatyam, [advayānutpādasatyam,] advayābhinirhārānmārgajñānāvatārasatyam, sarvākārābhisaṃbodhaḥ sarvabodhisattvabhūmikramānusaṃdhiniṣpādanatayāyāvattathāgatajñānasamudayasatyaṃ prajānāti /" ityuktavat /
body.translated_text: "The teaching of <s>Dharma</s> by the <s>Buddhas</s> relies upon two truths: the conventional truth of the world and ultimate truth." Thus it is stated. Therefore, if it is asked: apart from these two truths, do there exist other four noble truths? It is explained: Although this is so, nevertheless, for the purpose of teaching the causal and resultant nature of what is to be abandoned and what is to be adopted separately, the four noble truths are stated here. Therein, the category to be abandoned is defilement (<s>saṃkleśa</s>). Its result is the truth of suffering (<s>duḥkhasatya</s>). Its cause is the truth of origination (<s>samudayasatya</s>). The category to be adopted is purification (<s>vyavadāna</s>). Its result is the truth of cessation (<s>nirodhasatya</s>). The cause for attaining that is the truth of the path (<s>mārgasatya</s>). Therein, the truths of suffering, origination, and path are included within conventional truth (<s>saṃvṛtisatya</s>). The truth of cessation is the essential nature of ultimate truth (<s>paramārthasatya</s>). Whatever other truth there may be beyond these is also to be determined as included, as appropriate, within the two truths. If asked whether there exists yet another truth beyond the four truths, it is explained: As stated regarding the fifth <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage: "He knows as it really is: 'This is the noble truth of suffering.' He knows as it really is: 'This is the noble truth of the origination of suffering.' He knows as it really is: 'This is the noble truth of the cessation of suffering.' He knows as it really is: 'This is the noble truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering.' He becomes skilled in conventional truth (<s>saṃvṛtisatya</s>). He becomes skilled in ultimate truth (<s>paramārthasatya</s>). He becomes skilled in the truth of characteristics (<s>lakṣaṇasatya</s>). He becomes skilled in the truth of classification (<s>vibhāgasatya</s>). He becomes skilled in the truth of analysis (<s>nistīraṇasatya</s>). He becomes skilled in the truth of things (<s>vastusatya</s>). He becomes skilled in the truth of origination (<s>prabhavasatya</s>). He becomes skilled in the truth of cessation and non-arising (<s>kṣayānutpādasatya</s>). He becomes skilled in the truth of entering the knowledge of the path (<s>mārgajñānāvatārasatya</s>). He becomes skilled in the truth of the arising of <s>Tathāgata</s> knowledge by accomplishing the successive connection of all <s>Bodhisattva</s> stages. He knows conventional truth through satisfying other beings according to their aspirations. He knows ultimate truth through convergence upon a single mode of understanding. He knows the truth of characteristics through awakening to specific and general characteristics. He knows the truth of classification through awakening to the distinctions and arrangements of <s>dharmas</s>. He knows the truth of analysis through awakening to the arrangements of the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases). He knows the truth of things because of the impinging affliction of mind and body. He knows the truth of origination because of the connection between states of existence and intermediate states. He knows the truth of cessation and non-arising because of the complete and final pacification of the burning of all fevers. [He knows the truth of non-dual non-arising.] He knows the truth of entering the knowledge of the path through non-dual accomplishment. He knows the truth of the arising of <s>Tathāgata</s> knowledge through the complete awakening to all aspects, by accomplishing the successive connection of all <s>Bodhisattva</s> stages." Thus it is stated.

body.text: iti madhyamakāvatārabhāṣye sudurjayākhyaḥ pañcamaścittotpādaḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Madhyamakāvatārabhāṣya</s>, the fifth arising of the mind, called <s>Sudurjayā</s> (Difficult to Conquer).
